entry.title: 'You are not alone': Port St. Lucie woman turns grief into community for others
entry.summary: Losing someone you love can change everything. For Stacey Comer, that loss came in 2018 when her husband, Chris, died following complications from a kidney transplant. WATCH You Are Not Alone: PSL woman turns grief into community for others You Are Not Alone: PSL woman turns grief into community for others As she learned to navigate life without him, Comer also began to notice there wasn't one central place on the Treasure Coast where people experiencing grief could go to find support, resources and connection. She started asking herself a simple question: Why isn't there an entity where all of this lives under? That question became the foundation for Chriss Place , a free, in-person grief support community Comer is now creating on the Treasure Coast. Comer said grief can be difficult to understand until you experience it yourself. She added that while friends and family often want to help, people who are grieving can still feel isolated. You only sort of know it if you're in the club, and when you're in the club everyone wants to be so supportive and helpful, Comer said. Chriss Place is intended to give people a place to connect with others who understand what they're going through. The community is not limited to people who have lost a spouse or immediate family member. Comer wants it to be available to anyone who has experienced a loss and needs support navigating what comes next. Right now, Comer is creating Chriss Place from the ground up. Her long-term vision is to create a physical space on the Treasure Coast somewhere that feels comfortable and welcoming, where people can gather, find resources and connect with others who understand grief. You are not alone. You feel alone because you think you're the only one feeling it, but you're not, Comer said. For Comer, Chriss Place is rooted in the loss of her husband but she hopes it can become something much bigger. She wants other people on the Treasure Coast to have the kind of support she realized was missing during her own journey through grief. The ultimate goal is to create a community where people don't have to navigate that journey by themselves. While grief may look different for everyone, Comer wants people to know one thing: They don't have to face it alone. For more information on the next free community grief meet-up, visit their website .

entry.title: Port St. Lucie weighs mobility plan for future growth - cw34.com
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie weighs mobility plan for future growth    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Years of rapid growth have brought thousands of new homes, businesses and drivers to Port St. Now, city leaders are confronting the cost of keeping everyone moving: approximately $2.2 billion. Council members on Monday approved Ordinance 26-89 on first reading, moving forward the city’s 2050 Mobility Plan , an updated mobility-fee schedule and guidelines for administering the program. The plan serves as a 25-year roadmap for new and wider roads, intersection improvements, sidewalks, trails, bicycle facilities and transit. It does not, however, guarantee every project will be built. Approximately $1.7 billion of the plan is currently unfunded. We know there is not enough money to fund every single project in the mobility plan, a presenter told council during Monday’s meeting. The plan comes as Port St. Lucie has grown to more than 260,000 residents spread across approximately 120 square miles. City officials said the updated plan is intended to identify the transportation infrastructure that continued residential and commercial growth will require through 2050. Major road projects proposed by 2030 The plan divides proposed work into short-, mid- and long-term periods. The short-term plan, covering projects targeted through 2030, carries an estimated cost of approximately $403 million. Among the proposed short-term projects: Widen St. Lucie West Boulevard from four lanes to six between Interstate 95 and Cashmere Boulevard. Widen Torino Parkway from two lanes to four between Midway Road and Cashmere Boulevard. Widen California Boulevard from two lanes to four between St. Lucie West Boulevard and Crosstown Parkway. Lucie Boulevard from two lanes to four between Paar Drive and the Martin County line. Continue improvements along Floresta Drive between Prima Vista Boulevard and Crosstown Parkway. Widen Village Green Drive between Walton Road and Tiffany Avenue. Build or extend several roads intended to improve connections through growing areas of the city. Those projects remain part of a planning document. Their inclusion does not mean funding has been secured or construction will be completed by 2030. City officials also highlighted work already completed, underway or moving through design under the existing mobility program. That includes: A roundabout and widening near East Torino Parkway and Midway Road. Lucie Boulevard between Darwin and Gatlin boulevards. New sidewalks along Savage Boulevard and Selvitz Road. A sidewalk under construction on Kestor Drive. Traffic-calming improvements on Whitmore Drive. A feasibility study for improvements along St. An intersection project at Savona and Gatlin boulevards, with construction anticipated in 2027. Intersection improvements at Tradition and Village parkways. New development would pay more To help fund future projects, the ordinance updates the city’s mobility fees one-time charges tied to new development, redevelopment, additions and certain changes in property use. The fees are paid by developers, contractors or owner-builders, not existing homeowners. Developers could, however, factor the added expense into the prices of new homes, rents or commercial projects. The increase is not a blanket 50% hike for every development. Rates vary depending on the type of project and the area of the city where it is built. Under the proposal, the difference between the current fee and the newly calculated rate would be divided into four steps. The city would impose 25% of that difference in 2027, 50% in 2028, 75% in 2029 and the full calculated rate in 2030. For example, the current fee for a new single-family home east of I-95 is approximately $1.60 per square foot, up to 3,500 square feet. Under the updated schedule, it would rise to $1.80 per square foot in 2027 and $2.40 per square foot in 2030. For a new 2,000-square-foot home, that would mean an increase from approximately $3,200 today to $3,600 in 2027 and $4,800 by 2030. One council member raised concerns Monday about balancing the city’s infrastructure needs with the potential effect that higher development costs could have on housing affordability. Broader than road construction Port St. Lucie has used mobility fees since 2021. According to the city’s plan, the program collected more than $30 million between 2022 and 2024. Unlike traditional road impact fees, the money can support a broader range of transportation projects, including sidewalks, shared-use paths, trails, bicycle lanes, transit stops, mobility hubs and intersection improvements. The new plan extends the city’s previous transportation-planning horizon from 2045 to 2050. City officials said its short-, mid- and long-term road projects, multimodal improvements, intersection projects and transit plans remain largely unchanged from a version previously presented to council. The city held public workshops on the plan and proposed fee schedule Sept. 2 and 3 to gather input from residents, developers and other stakeholders. Because Monday’s vote was the ordinance’s first reading, it must return to City Council for final approval. If adopted, the ordinance and updated fee schedule would take effect Dec. entry.title: 'Let it go': Port St. Lucie police chief talks about road rage incident that ended with gunfire - WPBF
entry.summary: 'Let it go': Port St. Lucie police chief talks about road rage incident that ended with gunfire    WPBF
entry.article_text: More details are being released about a road rage incident in Port St. Lucie that escalated into a shooting Thursday evening, resulting in one man being injured and both drivers arrested on felony charges. Lucie police received a 911 call around 6:30 p.m. reporting gunshots in a residential neighborhood near SW California Boulevard and SW Brevity Terrace. "Gunshots in front of my house," a caller said during the emergency call. The caller also described the aftermath of the shooting. "I heard it, and then I saw a guy raising his hands up and said he had blood on his hands," the caller said. Investigators said the altercation began as a misunderstanding during a lane change and merge near SW Crosstown Parkway. The situation escalated into a physical confrontation when 41-year-old Dean Plotts exited his vehicle, approached 57-year-old Tylon Kukielka, who was seated in his car, and punched him through the window. "He stepped out of his vehicle, approached the other man who was seated inside his vehicle, and punched him inside his vehicle, so now he's breaking the plane of the window," the Port St. Lucie police chief Leo Niemczyk said. "Therefore, entering, which makes it a burglary of the conveyance with the intention of committing a crime, being battery by punching the other individual who is seated inside the vehicle." Plotts then returned to his vehicle, but the confrontation escalated further. "Almost makes it back to his vehicle and starts getting fire on," Niemczyk said. Police said Kukielka fired a handgun, striking Plotts twice. Both men were arrested, with Plotts facing charges for initiating the physical altercation and Kukielka for firing his weapon. When asked if Kukielka’s actions could be considered self-defense, Niemczyk said, "It's not self-defense at that point. If Plotts had been coming at him at that point, the shooting may well have been justified, but it was actually just the reverse. He was fleeing from him." Both men are now facing felony charges. Because one thought the other one may have cut the other one off when they were both turning into the same roadway. Again, no reason to be facing felony charges; let it go, let it go," Niemczyk said. entry.article_text: Jennifer Eckhart, a popular podcaster and former associate producer at Fox Business, died by suicide at her home in Hobe Sound on Saturday morning, according to the Martin County sheriff. Sheriff John Budensiek said he usually doesn't comment on suicides but decided to speak publicly about Eckhart’s death to address conspiracy theories suggesting she had been murdered. "Looking at the scene and going through the investigation, we spent a lot of time. We investigated it as if it was a homicide. Unfortunately, she took her life at her own hands," Budensiek said. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Eckhart gained notoriety after accusing a Fox News anchor of raping her. Investigators said she had family and friends who tried to help her, but she had been in and out of mental health facilities and had stopped taking her medications. If you'd like to talk to someone at 211 Helpline of Palm Beach and Treasure Coast, you can dial 211. If you'd like to text the helpline, you can message your ZIP code to 898211. Elizabeth Burrows, director of development and communications with 211 Palm Beach and Treasure Coast, emphasized the tragedy of suicide and encouraged those struggling to seek help. "Every death by suicide is a tragedy," Burrows said. She noted that anyone in crisis can call 211 or 988, which are available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, to provide resources or someone to talk to. "You'd be surprised at how often just having someone who's there to listen can help someone make it through their darkest moments," Burrows said. Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app. Burrows also stressed the importance of being present and asking questions when supporting someone who may be struggling. Asking about it does not make suicide more of a risk for them. If anything, it lets that person know that they are not alone," she said. "The one answer I can always give is to never give up. As long as someone is still here, there is still an opportunity to support and assist them." The sheriff said Eckhart’s death remains an open investigation as they await toxicology results, but he emphasized that all evidence points to suicide. If you or someone you know is struggling, help is available by dialing 211 or 988 for confidential support and resources. entry.summary: Man armed with knives shot outside Port St. Lucie Pollo Tropical later charged, police say    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A confrontation in a Port St. Lucie Pollo Tropical parking lot ended with a man shot in the upper torso and later facing charges. 19, officers with the Port St. Lucie Police Department responded to the Pollo Tropical at 1635 NW St. Lucie West Blvd., where they found Christopher Harris suffering from gunshot wounds to his upper torso, according to a news release. The shooting led to a heavy law enforcement investigation outside the business , with crime scene tape around the restaurant. The other person involved, identified as Isaiah Davis, 25, was detained at the scene while officers investigated. Police also recovered and secured a firearm. PSLPD said interviews and surveillance video from the restaurant showed the confrontation between Harris and Davis began after the two men had an interaction in the parking lot. Davis entered the restaurant to pick up a delivery order, and Harris followed him inside despite not appearing to place or pick up an order, police said. When Davis left the restaurant, Harris allegedly followed him outside. Police said surveillance video showed Harris, who was armed with a knife, push Davis and then advance toward him as Davis backed away. Davis then pulled out a gun and fired one round, striking Harris in the upper torso, according to PSLPD. Harris returned to the restaurant, where people began rendering aid and called 911. See also: Causeway Cove project fight escalates: Can Fort Pierce push back against state law? During the investigation, officers recovered one knife from Harris' waistband while aid was being provided and another from his front pocket, police said. Harris was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital for treatment. Based on surveillance video, witness statements and other evidence, detectives determined Harris was the primary aggressor, according to PSLPD. He was charged with attempted aggravated battery with a deadly weapon and felony battery based on a prior battery conviction. Police said Harris will be booked into the St. Lucie County Jail once he is medically released from the hospital.

WATCH: Indiantown 'Project Silver Fox' data center plan returns with changes, resident concerns remainThe debate over the project highlights a familiar tension in growing communities: the promise of economic development versus the desire to maintain a community’s character, with a final decision by the Village Council expected to shape Indiantown's future for years to come.The project was initially withdrawn in April. Now, developers say they have directly addressed the public’s biggest worries.Adam Kramer, an executive with Project Silver Fox, said the new plan includes several key commitments intended to mitigate the facility's impact.“It’s a waterless data center,” Kramer stated, emphasizing that the project would not use Indiantown’s water resources. He also noted changes to the facility’s design and footprint. “We have commitments on how we are doing natural landscaping with retaining the trees there to kind of block the view of the data center, working on the size of the facility.”The project is slated for land already zoned for industrial use, the former site of a power plant. According to project officials, noise levels will remain within village code, there will be no ongoing vibrations, and local water pressure will not be affected.Proponents of the data center point to its potential to transform the local economy without costing taxpayers. Kramer said the project could represent a billion-dollar investment in the village.“What the project is, is an economic opportunity for the community and creating jobs, creating tax revenue,” Kramer said.That view is shared by Kloee Ciuperger, the CEO of the Economic Council of Indiantown.“I think a huge part of the benefits is gonna be that tax revenue,” Ciuperger said. “That’s gonna be able to go to youth, athletics, to parks, to the water infrastructure, to the wastewater infrastructure.”However, some residents at the open house remained skeptical of the developers' motives.“This is a money grab, a land grab and we do not want this,” said Penny Kaminsky-Preli. Despite the proposed changes, many who attended the meeting voiced continuing concerns about the impact of a large-scale data center on their daily lives.Penny Kaminsky-Preli, an Indiantown resident, said the facility is too close to homes and a local school.“First of all they’re way too close to people. entry.title: Port St. Lucie weighs mobility plan for future growth - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie weighs mobility plan for future growth    WPEC
entry.article_text: Years of rapid growth have brought thousands of new homes, businesses and drivers to Port St. Now, city leaders are confronting the cost of keeping everyone moving: approximately $2.2 billion. Council members on Monday approved Ordinance 26-89 on first reading, moving forward the city’s 2050 Mobility Plan , an updated mobility-fee schedule and guidelines for administering the program. The plan serves as a 25-year roadmap for new and wider roads, intersection improvements, sidewalks, trails, bicycle facilities and transit. It does not, however, guarantee every project will be built. Approximately $1.7 billion of the plan is currently unfunded. We know there is not enough money to fund every single project in the mobility plan, a presenter told council during Monday’s meeting. The plan comes as Port St. Lucie has grown to more than 260,000 residents spread across approximately 120 square miles. City officials said the updated plan is intended to identify the transportation infrastructure that continued residential and commercial growth will require through 2050. Major road projects proposed by 2030 The plan divides proposed work into short-, mid- and long-term periods. The short-term plan, covering projects targeted through 2030, carries an estimated cost of approximately $403 million. Among the proposed short-term projects: Widen St. Lucie West Boulevard from four lanes to six between Interstate 95 and Cashmere Boulevard. Widen Torino Parkway from two lanes to four between Midway Road and Cashmere Boulevard. Widen California Boulevard from two lanes to four between St. Lucie West Boulevard and Crosstown Parkway. Lucie Boulevard from two lanes to four between Paar Drive and the Martin County line. Continue improvements along Floresta Drive between Prima Vista Boulevard and Crosstown Parkway. Widen Village Green Drive between Walton Road and Tiffany Avenue. Build or extend several roads intended to improve connections through growing areas of the city. Those projects remain part of a planning document. Their inclusion does not mean funding has been secured or construction will be completed by 2030. City officials also highlighted work already completed, underway or moving through design under the existing mobility program. That includes: A roundabout and widening near East Torino Parkway and Midway Road. Lucie Boulevard between Darwin and Gatlin boulevards. New sidewalks along Savage Boulevard and Selvitz Road. A sidewalk under construction on Kestor Drive. Traffic-calming improvements on Whitmore Drive. A feasibility study for improvements along St. An intersection project at Savona and Gatlin boulevards, with construction anticipated in 2027. Intersection improvements at Tradition and Village parkways. New development would pay more To help fund future projects, the ordinance updates the city’s mobility fees one-time charges tied to new development, redevelopment, additions and certain changes in property use. The fees are paid by developers, contractors or owner-builders, not existing homeowners. Developers could, however, factor the added expense into the prices of new homes, rents or commercial projects. The increase is not a blanket 50% hike for every development. Rates vary depending on the type of project and the area of the city where it is built. Under the proposal, the difference between the current fee and the newly calculated rate would be divided into four steps. The city would impose 25% of that difference in 2027, 50% in 2028, 75% in 2029 and the full calculated rate in 2030. For example, the current fee for a new single-family home east of I-95 is approximately $1.60 per square foot, up to 3,500 square feet. Under the updated schedule, it would rise to $1.80 per square foot in 2027 and $2.40 per square foot in 2030. For a new 2,000-square-foot home, that would mean an increase from approximately $3,200 today to $3,600 in 2027 and $4,800 by 2030. One council member raised concerns Monday about balancing the city’s infrastructure needs with the potential effect that higher development costs could have on housing affordability. Broader than road construction Port St. Lucie has used mobility fees since 2021. According to the city’s plan, the program collected more than $30 million between 2022 and 2024. Unlike traditional road impact fees, the money can support a broader range of transportation projects, including sidewalks, shared-use paths, trails, bicycle lanes, transit stops, mobility hubs and intersection improvements. The new plan extends the city’s previous transportation-planning horizon from 2045 to 2050. City officials said its short-, mid- and long-term road projects, multimodal improvements, intersection projects and transit plans remain largely unchanged from a version previously presented to council. The city held public workshops on the plan and proposed fee schedule Sept. 2 and 3 to gather input from residents, developers and other stakeholders. Because Monday’s vote was the ordinance’s first reading, it must return to City Council for final approval. If adopted, the ordinance and updated fee schedule would take effect Dec. entry.title: Causeway Cove project fight escalates: Can Fort Pierce push back against state law? - WPEC
entry.summary: Causeway Cove project fight escalates: Can Fort Pierce push back against state law?    WPEC
entry.article_text: A proposed luxury waterfront development in Fort Pierce is drawing renewed attention after city commissioners approved a motion to explore hiring outside legal counsel to review whether the city has any options to challenge the project under Florida's Live Local Act. 14 vote comes as cities across Florida continue testing the limits of the state's Live Local Act and lawmakers implement the latest round of changes to the law. The proposed Causeway Cove development on South Hutchinson Island has become one of the Treasure Coast's most closely watched growth disputes, putting residents and local officials at odds with a state law that limits how much control cities have over certain housing projects. 14 meeting, the commission approved a motion to explore hiring an outside land-use attorney to determine whether Fort Pierce has any legal grounds to challenge the project under the Live Local Act. The city is also monitoring lawsuits filed elsewhere in Florida that seek to restore greater local control over development decisions. The move comes as Florida enters the latest phase of the law. Known as Live Local 4.0, the most recent changes took effect July 1, 2026, expanding eligible development sites and further clarifying protections for qualifying projects that include affordable housing. Qualifying developments must continue to reserve at least 40% of units as affordable rental housing for at least 30 years. Now, Fort Pierce finds itself at the center of a broader statewide debate over growth, affordable housing and home rule. The proposed redevelopment would dramatically transform the Causeway Cove property along Seaway Drive. According to city records, plans call for five towers ranging from 11 to 17 stories, 913 residential units, two hotels totaling 407 rooms, more than 72,000 square feet of retail and commercial space, and 218 marina slips. For residents like Edie Harrison, the project would change the area known for its waterfront views, boating access and small-town character. "Everything is still very quaint," Harrison said. "It's one of those gems." Harrison and hundreds of other residents have raised concerns about the size of the development, traffic impacts and what they view as a lack of public input. At the center of the fight is Florida's Live Local Act, a law passed in 2023 to encourage the construction of affordable and workforce housing across the state. The law allows qualifying projects to bypass certain local zoning, density and height restrictions if affordability requirements are met. City officials have repeatedly said the proposed Causeway Cove project qualifies under the law and therefore moves through an administrative review process rather than a traditional public hearing and commission vote. For critics, that process has become one of the most controversial aspects of the proposal. Fort Pierce Commissioner Michael Broderick said residents' concerns extend beyond the size of the development. "The concern is density, traffic flow," Broderick said, pointing to longstanding concerns about capacity on Seaway Drive. Another major debate centers on affordability. Under Live Local, affordable housing calculations are based on regional income levels rather than income levels specific to Fort Pierce. Critics argue the formula can produce rents that technically qualify as affordable under state guidelines but remain difficult for many local residents to afford. According to city officials, some qualifying units could rent for more than $2,300 per month, while Fort Pierce's median rent is substantially lower. Broderick said many residents question whether those figures reflect true affordability within the city. Even some lawmakers who supported the legislation have raised concerns about how it is being applied. Dana Trabulsy, whose district includes parts of the Treasure Coast, has recently questioned whether developments of this scale reflect what legislators intended when they approved the measure. The Fort Pierce dispute is also part of a much larger battle unfolding across Florida. Several lawsuits challenging aspects of the Live Local Act are moving through the courts as cities seek to regain greater authority over local development decisions. Supporters of the law argue it is helping address Florida's housing shortage, while critics contend it has weakened local home-rule powers and limited communities' ability to shape growth. Land-use attorney Keith Poliakoff, who has represented clients in Live Local disputes across the state, said local governments generally have limited discretion once a project satisfies state requirements. Poliakoff said the law effectively requires municipalities to administratively approve qualifying projects, even when residents or local leaders oppose the density, height or scale of a development. State data show more than 200 Live Local projects have been proposed or approved across Florida , making the law one of the most significant growth and housing measures enacted in recent years. Related 2024 article: $100M Kanner Hwy development in Stuart: Affordable housing powered by Live Local Act If things move forward as anticipated, construction on the Causeway Cove development could begin before the end of the year. The property's owner, Palm Beach developer Ashton DePeyster, did not respond to requests for comment. This report is part of an ongoing CBS12 News I-Team investigation examining the impact of Florida's Live Local Act, the legal challenges surrounding the law, and how communities across the Treasure Coast are responding to large-scale development projects.

entry.title: Armed, dangerous person leaves Palm City residence after shots fired, sheriff's office says - WPBF
entry.summary: Armed, dangerous person leaves Palm City residence after shots fired, sheriff's office says    WPBF
entry.article_text: A man barricaded with a weapon inside a residence in Palm City was taken into custody after he chased his girlfriend down the road with a gun Saturday afternoon, the Martin County Sheriff’s Office said. Darrel Abbey, 38, was apprehended after leaving the home on Southwest Bessey Creek Trail near Murphy Road, the sheriff's office posted on Facebook. "The Martin County Sheriff’s Office SWAT Team has safely resolved the armed barricaded subject situation on Southwest Bessey Creek Trail," the agency said. He was taken to the Martin County Jail and booked at 6:57 p.m. He is facing three charges: felony aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill (domestic), misdemeanor battery (domestic) and misdemeanor use of a firearm under the influence of alcohol. https://www.facebook.com/MartinCountySheriffsOffice/posts/pfbid0UhZCMdUMpppSpxntWNQ2nc5uVBuTDK6zfE7YKBDU9gjfPz4XcNqwzeLRwj8kP6jbl Shortly after 3 p.m., the sheriff's office took a call from a frantic woman who said she was chased down the street by a man, who went into the backyard and fired multiple shots, Sheriff John Budensiek told WPBF's Caleb Califano at the scene. He said he threatened to kill her. Multiple people around the neighborhood then called 911. Callers indicated the incident was domestic-related and involved an aggravated assault with a deadly weapon inside the residence, the sheriff's office said. The man was described as "armed and dangerous" inside the home. Sheriff's office road patrol, detectives, SWAT and the hostage negotiation team were on the scene working to safely resolve the situation, the agency said. "He wouldn't talk to them," Budensiek said. "So eventually our SWAT team was called to this location to try to resolve this scenario peacefully. "But this is where all the tools and the resources that we have come into play to keep the county residents safe." The SWAT team used a loudspeaker to order him out. When he refused, the sheriff's office pumped gas into the house. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25

entry.summary: Former Fox News producer Jennifer Eckhart dies by suicide in Martin County    WPBF
entry.article_text: Jennifer Eckhart, a popular podcaster and former associate producer at Fox Business, died by suicide at her home in Hobe Sound on Saturday morning, according to the Martin County sheriff. Sheriff John Budensiek said he usually doesn't comment on suicides but decided to speak publicly about Eckhart’s death to address conspiracy theories suggesting she had been murdered. "Looking at the scene and going through the investigation, we spent a lot of time. We investigated it as if it was a homicide. Unfortunately, she took her life at her own hands," Budensiek said. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Eckhart gained notoriety after accusing a Fox News anchor of raping her. Investigators said she had family and friends who tried to help her, but she had been in and out of mental health facilities and had stopped taking her medications. If you'd like to talk to someone at 211 Helpline of Palm Beach and Treasure Coast, you can dial 211. If you'd like to text the helpline, you can message your ZIP code to 898211. Elizabeth Burrows, director of development and communications with 211 Palm Beach and Treasure Coast, emphasized the tragedy of suicide and encouraged those struggling to seek help. "Every death by suicide is a tragedy," Burrows said. She noted that anyone in crisis can call 211 or 988, which are available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, to provide resources or someone to talk to. "You'd be surprised at how often just having someone who's there to listen can help someone make it through their darkest moments," Burrows said. Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app. Burrows also stressed the importance of being present and asking questions when supporting someone who may be struggling. Asking about it does not make suicide more of a risk for them. If anything, it lets that person know that they are not alone," she said. "The one answer I can always give is to never give up. As long as someone is still here, there is still an opportunity to support and assist them." The sheriff said Eckhart’s death remains an open investigation as they await toxicology results, but he emphasized that all evidence points to suicide. If you or someone you know is struggling, help is available by dialing 211 or 988 for confidential support and resources. If you or someone you know needs help, you can talk with the Suicide Crisis Lifeline by calling or sending a text message to 988, or you can chat online here.

entry.title: 'You are not alone': Port St. Lucie woman turns grief into community for others - WPTV
entry.summary: 'You are not alone': Port St. Lucie woman turns grief into community for others    WPTV
entry.article_text: Losing someone you love can change everything.For Stacey Comer, that loss came in 2018 when her husband, Chris, died following complications from a kidney transplant.WATCH ‘You Are Not Alone’: PSL woman turns grief into community for othersAs she learned to navigate life without him, Comer also began to notice there wasn't one central place on the Treasure Coast where people experiencing grief could go to find support, resources and connection.She started asking herself a simple question: “Why isn't there an entity where all of this lives under?”That question became the foundation for Chris’s Place, a free, in-person grief support community Comer is now creating on the Treasure Coast.Comer said grief can be difficult to understand until you experience it yourself. She added that while friends and family often want to help, people who are grieving can still feel isolated.“You only sort of know it if you're in the club, and when you're in the club everyone wants to be so supportive and helpful,” Comer said.Chris’s Place is intended to give people a place to connect with others who understand what they're going through.The community is not limited to people who have lost a spouse or immediate family member. Comer wants it to be available to anyone who has experienced a loss and needs support navigating what comes next.Right now, Comer is creating Chris’s Place from the ground up.Her long-term vision is to create a physical space on the Treasure Coast — somewhere that feels comfortable and welcoming, where people can gather, find resources and connect with others who understand grief.“You are not alone. You feel alone because you think you're the only one feeling it, but you're not,” Comer said.For Comer, Chris’s Place is rooted in the loss of her husband — but she hopes it can become something much bigger.She wants other people on the Treasure Coast to have the kind of support she realized was missing during her own journey through grief.The ultimate goal is to create a community where people don't have to navigate that journey by themselves. While grief may look different for everyone, Comer wants people to know one thing: They don't have to face it alone.For more information on the next free community grief meet-up, visit their website.

entry.title: Indian River County sheriff announces 50+ arrests in multi-agency human trafficking operation - WPTV
entry.summary: Indian River County sheriff announces 50+ arrests in multi-agency human trafficking operation    WPTV
entry.article_text: The Indian River County Sheriff's Office announced more than 50 arrests following a multi-agency, multi-day operation targeting human trafficking and illegal sexual activity in the county.WATCH BELOW: Indian River County Sheriff's Office reveals results of multi-agency operationOperation Late Checkout ran from Sept. 13 in Indian River County. The operation netted over 60 contacts, more than 50 arrests, and three ICE detainers, Sheriff Eric Flowers said during a press conference on Thursday.Flowers announced the results alongside a representative from the Florida Department of Law Enforcement."Agencies involved in the operation included the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Florida Department of Law Enforcement, St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Seminole County Sheriff's Office, Altamonte Springs Police Department, Vero Beach Police Department, Homeland Security Investigations, Florida Office of Statewide Prosecutor and the U.S. Attorney's Office," Flowers said.The operation's targeted goal was stopping human trafficking in the Indian River County area, the sheriff's office said.During the operation, several victims were identified, and investigators said ongoing investigations are underway. Flowers said there are no specific arrests on human trafficking charges at this time.One case involved a man who traveled to Indian River County to meet a minor. Flowers said the arrest was the result of the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force working across agencies to apprehend individuals attempting to lure children online."Our team did a great job of getting him off the street," Flowers said.Undercover teams were deployed in a variety of capacities during the operation, the sheriff's office said. Victims' advocates trained to work with trafficking victims were also on hand to speak with women involved in prostitution to determine whether they were being trafficked."We have many ongoing investigations as a result of this," Flowers said.Flowers called the operation unprecedented for Indian River County."We've never had an investigation like this, to my knowledge, in Indian River County with this many agencies involved, with this many arrests in one shot," he said.FDLE Assistant Special Agent in Charge Alfonso Williams said Operation Late Checkout was initiated by FDLE in coordination with the Indian River County Sheriff's Office and is the first operation of this magnitude conducted in the county."This operation shows that within our communities there are dangerous individuals committing heinous crimes who think they can get away with it," Williams said.Williams said the operation focused on identifying human trafficking victims, reducing the demand for prostitution, and apprehending individuals seeking sexual contact with minors."Our work is far from done," Williams said. "This operation requires a lot of resources and time. We cannot do this work alone, and our success depends on the great partnership and collaboration that you see today."FDLE said it houses the Florida Trafficking Hotline. entry.title: 3 juveniles arrested in connection to deadly shooting of 17-year-old girl in Riviera Beach
entry.summary: Three juveniles have been arrested in connection with the deadly shooting of a 17-year-old girl in Riviera Beach last month, according to the Riviera Beach Police Department. Police announced on Monday that the U.S. Marshals Service took the suspects into custody for the Aug. 21 shooting that occurred in the 1400 block of West 36th Street shortly after 8 p.m. All three now face first-degree murder charges. WATCH THE PRESS CONFERENCE STARTING AT 9 A.M.: Detectives determined the three juveniles conspired to commit a robbery that ultimately led to the victim's death. The alleged shooter faces charges including first-degree premeditated murder with a firearm, principal in the first degree and tampering with a witness, victim or informant. The two accomplices each face first-degree murder, principal in the first degree, and attempted armed robbery charges. Flock camera and License Plate Reader (LPR) technology was used to track the suspect vehicle as it fled the scene immediately after the shooting. 'These are senseless acts of violence, and the department is committed to stopping them,' said Police Chief Michael A. Coleman. 'In this case, the individuals involved are juveniles. This behavior cannot continue, and our community deserves better.' The investigation remains active. Anyone with additional information is urged to contact the Riviera Beach Police Department at 561-845-4123 or submit an anonymous tip through Crime Stoppers at 1-800-458-TIPS (8477).

entry.title: 'Let it go': Port St. Lucie police chief talks about road rage incident that ended with gunfire - wpbf.com
entry.summary: 'Let it go': Port St. Lucie police chief talks about road rage incident that ended with gunfire    wpbf.com
entry.article_text: More details are being released about a road rage incident in Port St. Lucie that escalated into a shooting Thursday evening, resulting in one man being injured and both drivers arrested on felony charges. Lucie police received a 911 call around 6:30 p.m. reporting gunshots in a residential neighborhood near SW California Boulevard and SW Brevity Terrace. "Gunshots in front of my house," a caller said during the emergency call. The caller also described the aftermath of the shooting. "I heard it, and then I saw a guy raising his hands up and said he had blood on his hands," the caller said. Investigators said the altercation began as a misunderstanding during a lane change and merge near SW Crosstown Parkway. The situation escalated into a physical confrontation when 41-year-old Dean Plotts exited his vehicle, approached 57-year-old Tylon Kukielka, who was seated in his car, and punched him through the window. "He stepped out of his vehicle, approached the other man who was seated inside his vehicle, and punched him inside his vehicle, so now he's breaking the plane of the window," the Port St. Lucie police chief Leo Niemczyk said. "Therefore, entering, which makes it a burglary of the conveyance with the intention of committing a crime, being battery by punching the other individual who is seated inside the vehicle." Plotts then returned to his vehicle, but the confrontation escalated further. "Almost makes it back to his vehicle and starts getting fire on," Niemczyk said. Police said Kukielka fired a handgun, striking Plotts twice. Both men were arrested, with Plotts facing charges for initiating the physical altercation and Kukielka for firing his weapon. When asked if Kukielka’s actions could be considered self-defense, Niemczyk said, "It's not self-defense at that point. If Plotts had been coming at him at that point, the shooting may well have been justified, but it was actually just the reverse. He was fleeing from him." Both men are now facing felony charges. Because one thought the other one may have cut the other one off when they were both turning into the same roadway. Again, no reason to be facing felony charges; let it go, let it go," Niemczyk said. entry.summary: Man shot outside Port St. Lucie Pollo Tropical now faces charges, police say    wpbf.com
entry.article_text: A 37-year-old man who was shot during a confrontation outside a Pollo Tropical in Port St. Lucie is now facing charges after investigators determined he was the primary aggressor in the encounter, according to police. Lucie Police Department said officers responded around 3:43 p.m. 19, to the restaurant at 1365 NW St. Lucie West Boulevard after receiving reports of a shooting. When officers arrived, they found Christopher Harris, 37, suffering from a gunshot wound to his upper torso. He was flown to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where his injuries were determined to be non-life-threatening, police said. The other person involved, identified by police as Isaiah Davis, 25, was detained at the scene while detectives investigated. Officers also recovered a firearm. According to investigators, the encounter began after Harris and Davis had an interaction in the restaurant's parking lot. Police said surveillance video showed Davis entering the restaurant to pick up a food delivery order and Harris following him inside, despite Harris not appearing to place or pick up an order. Police said Harris then followed Davis back outside, where exterior surveillance video showed Harris pushing Davis and advancing toward him as Davis moved backward. Investigators said Harris was armed with a knife during the confrontation, and witnesses reported seeing him with a knife shortly before the shooting. Davis fired one round, striking Harris in the chest, according to police. Harris went back inside the restaurant, where people began providing aid and called 911. Investigators said one knife was recovered after it had been removed from Harris' waistband while people were helping him. Police said another knife was later found in his front pocket. After reviewing surveillance video, physical evidence and witness statements, detectives determined Harris was the primary aggressor and established probable cause to charge him with attempted aggravated battery with a deadly weapon and felony battery based on a prior battery conviction, according to the department. Because Harris remained hospitalized, police said an arrest affidavit was submitted to the St. He is expected to be booked into the jail after he is medically released. Police said no criminal charges are currently pending against Davis. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates

entry.summary: Former Fox News producer Jennifer Eckhart dies by suicide in Martin County    wpbf.com
entry.article_text: Jennifer Eckhart, a popular podcaster and former associate producer at Fox Business, died by suicide at her home in Hobe Sound on Saturday morning, according to the Martin County sheriff. Sheriff John Budensiek said he usually doesn't comment on suicides but decided to speak publicly about Eckhart’s death to address conspiracy theories suggesting she had been murdered. "Looking at the scene and going through the investigation, we spent a lot of time. We investigated it as if it was a homicide. Unfortunately, she took her life at her own hands," Budensiek said. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Eckhart gained notoriety after accusing a Fox News anchor of raping her. Investigators said she had family and friends who tried to help her, but she had been in and out of mental health facilities and had stopped taking her medications. If you'd like to talk to someone at 211 Helpline of Palm Beach and Treasure Coast, you can dial 211. If you'd like to text the helpline, you can message your ZIP code to 898211. Elizabeth Burrows, director of development and communications with 211 Palm Beach and Treasure Coast, emphasized the tragedy of suicide and encouraged those struggling to seek help. "Every death by suicide is a tragedy," Burrows said. She noted that anyone in crisis can call 211 or 988, which are available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, to provide resources or someone to talk to. "You'd be surprised at how often just having someone who's there to listen can help someone make it through their darkest moments," Burrows said. Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app. Burrows also stressed the importance of being present and asking questions when supporting someone who may be struggling. Asking about it does not make suicide more of a risk for them. If anything, it lets that person know that they are not alone," she said. "The one answer I can always give is to never give up. As long as someone is still here, there is still an opportunity to support and assist them." The sheriff said Eckhart’s death remains an open investigation as they await toxicology results, but he emphasized that all evidence points to suicide. If you or someone you know is struggling, help is available by dialing 211 or 988 for confidential support and resources. If you or someone you know needs help, you can talk with the Suicide Crisis Lifeline by calling or sending a text message to 988, or you can chat online here.

entry.title: Fort Pierce man arrested after raid of illicit drugs worth millions - wpbf.com
entry.summary: Fort Pierce man arrested after raid of illicit drugs worth millions    wpbf.com
entry.article_text: A Fort Pierce man was arrested after a raid Friday by the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office and U.S. Marshals Service found a massive amount of illicit drugs, including fentanyl and cocaine, worth several million dollars. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office Special Investigations Division, with assistance from the SWAT Team and the U.S. Marshals Service, executed a narcotics-related search warrant at a residence in the 3100 block of S. 24th Street in Fort Pierce. The subject of the investigation, Tony Saunders, 48, was taken into custody. Saunders, a three-time convicted felon who is on federal probation, also had two active warrants related to the sale and delivery of controlled substances. Afterward, Saunders faced additional charges of trafficking in fentanyl, trafficking in cocaine, trafficking in MDPV, manufacturing cocaine, tampering with evidence and possession of marijuana with intent to sell. https://www.facebook.com/stluciesheriff/posts/pfbid0j4igLYhtX4QpfPCZhHkYeREcfiqd9eehsAoAcjVwDWTipnXHZNWyrJLe6gbwukcvl The search resulted in the seizure of approximately 4.5 kilograms of fentanyl, 303 grams of cocaine, 97 grams of marijuana laced with MDPV, and 60 oxycodone pills totaling approximately 6.2 grams, the sheriff's office said. The street value of 4.5 kilograms of fentanyl can range from $150,000 to nearly $1.8 million, depending heavily on its purity, geographic location, and whether it is sold as wholesale powder or broken down into counterfeit pills, according to U.S. Customs and Border Protection. The estimated street value of 303 grams of cocaine in the U.S. ranges between roughly $18,180 and $60,600. Detectives also seized assorted ammunition, drug paraphernalia and materials consistent with the preparation and distribution of narcotics. A single kilogram of fentanyl has the potential to kill 500,000 people, making 4.5 kilograms a lethal volume capable of millions of fatal doses, according to the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration. “4.5 kilos of fentanyl are 4.5 kilos that will not reach our streets," Sheriff Richard Del Tro said. "Fentanyl is a deadly poison, and those who traffic in it are putting lives at risk for profit. I commend our detectives, SWAT Team, and the U.S. Marshals Service for their commitment to this mission. We will continue to pursue those who traffic dangerous narcotics and do everything within our authority to make St. Lucie County the safest county in Florida.” Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25

entry.title: Dolly Parton’s nephew fired from longtime security role, TMZ reports
entry.summary: Dolly Partons nephew, Bryan Seaver, has reportedly been fired from his longtime role overseeing security for the late country music legend. TMZ reported on Monday that it obtained a termination notice saying Seaver and his security companies had been immediately dismissed. TMZ also reported that a new security team has already taken over at Partons two Nashville homes, as well as her museum and warehouse. Seaver and his team told TMZ they were dismayed by the unexpected and, so far, unexplained actions. Their statement also criticized Partons longtime manager, Danny Nozell, and Pinnacle Bank. We remain unshakably resolved to fulfill her final directive to protect her family, and we refuse to be intimidated by those whose actions we believe are being taken in bad faith, and with the intent to profit from the life of someone who willingly gave so much, the statement said. Seaver is the son of Partons sister, Cassie, and served as his aunts head of security for more than two decades. His father, Larry, held the role before him. Seaver was also the person who announced Partons death in a video posted to her Instagram account on Aug. 25 . He said in the video that Parton had asked him years earlier to make the announcement when the time came. Parton died at 80 following a brief battle with cancer. Since her death, tributes honoring Partons life and legacy have continued. Plans are underway to rename Nashville International Airport in her honor, and the city will celebrate its first Dolly Day on Sept. 25.

entry.title: Missouri redistricting chaos continues as federal judges back disputed GOP map
entry.summary: A long-running legal fight over Missouris congressional map took another turn Monday when a federal appeals panel ruled in favor of new districts backed by President Donald Trump, even though the U.S. Supreme Court has blocked those districts from being used in the November election. A three-judge panel of the 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals said Missouri should use the new Republican-drawn U.S. House districts in the November election, just as the state did in its August primary. To revert to its prior districts for the general election would violate the U.S. Constitution, the appeals judges said. The appeals panel directed a lower court judge to issue a permanent injunction against using anything other than the map favored by Trump. But the ruling has no immediate impact. Thats because the panel also ordered the judge to delay the effect of the order for one week to allow time for an appeal. The judge quickly did so. Opponents of the new map said Monday that they will file an emergency appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court. The Supreme Court already has twice sided against the Trump-backed map. Earlier this month, it blocked enforcement of a lower court order favoring the new map pending a potential appeal and eventual decision by the high court. Missouri currently is set to run its November election with the same congressional districts it used in 2024 and 2022, following prior decisions by both the Missouri Supreme Court and the U.S. Supreme Court. Appeals panel ruling comes amid absentee voting Local elections officials already have sent absentee ballots to overseas citizens and military voters using the 2022 districts. State law requires absentee ballots to be available to all other voters by Tuesday. Local elections officials theoretically could scramble to change ballots again and could send replacements for ones already distributed. But if voters already have cast an absentee ballot, they cannot change their vote even if the district boundaries have changed. Miller County Clerk Clinton Jenkins said he mailed an absentee ballot Friday to a Missouri voter living in Australia and also sent ballots to other overseas voters. But he suggested that other people wait a little deeper into the absentee period, just in case the congressional district boundaries get swapped again. To try to change districts at this late date would be practically impossible and cost hundreds of thousands of dollars, the Missouri Association of County Clerks and Election Authoriti

Republicans hope the map could help them win seven of the state’s eight House seats — one more than they currently hold.Cleaver was unopposed in the Democratic primary, and Brattin won a multi-way Republican primary. Brattin praised Monday's appeals panel decision, saying that switching districts after the primary “defies common sense and undermines the entire electoral process.”RELATED STORY | Midterm voting picks up amid massive shifts in voting districtsAbout 59% of the 5th District's potential voters are new under the revised map, which also changes several other districts. All told, more than a million potential Missouri voters, or nearly 1 in 4 voters statewide, are affected by the redistricting, according to an Associated Press estimate.Missouri’s redistricting battle has been the longest and most complex among roughly a dozen states that sought to change their U.S. House districts over the past year.

entry.title: X-ray technician accused of sexually assaulting patient during MRI at HCA St. Lucie Hospital
entry.summary: A traveling X-ray technician has been accused of sexually assaulting a patient during an MRI procedure at HCA St. Lucie Medical Hospital, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department. Gabriel Cruz, 42, of Grant-Valkaria, was working as a contract technician at the hospital when the alleged assault occurred on Sept. 13. The victim, a female patient who was receiving treatment for fainting episodes, reported the incident to hospital administration the following day. According to the police report, the patient had been brought to the emergency room by her nephew on Sept. 11 for evaluation after experiencing fainting spells and head injuries. She underwent a CT scan and was scheduled for an MRI two days later to further assess her condition. The victim told investigators that Cruz made inappropriate comments before the procedure, allegedly telling her 'nobody can see what I can do to you.' During the MRI, the patient was given medication that made her drowsy. She reported waking up to find Cruz sexually assaulting her. Hospital security footage from Sept. 13 shows Cruz entering the MRI room with the patient and later exiting while carrying an unknown object and wearing purple latex gloves. The video confirms Cruz was the only person in the MRI room with the victim during the time period in question. According to the police report, Cruz had been working at the hospital on contract since August 2026. The case has been forwarded to the Criminal Investigation Division for further investigation. WPTV received this statement from HCA St. Lucie Medical Hospital on Sept. 17: We do not tolerate behavior that jeopardizes the safety or security of our patients. When this serious allegation was reported to us, we contacted law enforcement and ended the individuals assignment. We have assisted law enforcement throughout its investigation and remain focused on supporting our patient.

entry.title: 3 minors arrested in connection to deadly shooting of 17-year-old girl in Riviera Beach
entry.summary: Three minors have been arrested in connection with the fatal shooting of a 17-year-old girl in Riviera Beach, according to the Riviera Beach Police Department. The U.S. Marshals Service took the suspects into custody for the August 21 shooting, and all three now face first-degree murder charges. Riviera Beach Police Chief Michael A. Coleman held a press conference Tuesday morning to provide more details on the case. 'This was a heartbreaking loss for her family, her friends, and our community,' Coleman said. 'According to our investigation, three juveniles allegedly planned to rob the victim of a firearm she attempted to sell. That attempted robbery escalated into violence, and a young life was cut short.' WATCH THE FULL PRESS CONFERENCE BELOW: 3 minors arrested in connection to deadly shooting of 17-year-old girl in Riviera Beach Officers responded to the 1400 block of West 36th Street near Goodmark Park shortly after 8 p.m. and discovered the victim suffering from a gunshot wound to the head. Police determined the suspects, who knew the victim from the community but were not friends, communicated with her through social media to arrange the gun sale before attempting to rob her instead. The alleged shooter, a 17-year-old, faces first-degree premeditated murder with a firearm, principal in the first degree, and tampering with a witness, victim, or informant. Two accomplices, both 16, each face first-degree murder, principal in the first degree, and attempted armed robbery charges. One suspect was arrested in Jacksonville while two were taken into custody in Riviera Beach. Two of the three juveniles were previously known to law enforcement and had been in the system for several years, Coleman said. Advanced surveillance technology proved crucial in solving the case. Detectives used Flock camera and License Plate Reader technology to track the suspect vehicle as it fled the scene immediately after the shooting, following it to the suspects' homes. Coleman added that the department will continue using Flock cameras despite recent state restrictions on their use on state roads. 'We'll continue to use the Flock cameras until they go away, until the city leadership decide they don't no longer want them in the city,' Coleman said. 'They're invaluable to our investigation, how we use them.' Coleman emphasized that the investigation remains active and additional arrests may be forthcoming. Police determined the suspects, who knew the victim from the community but were not friends, communicated with her through social media to arrange the gun sale before attempting to rob her instead.The alleged shooter, a 17-year-old, faces first-degree premeditated murder with a firearm, principal in the first degree, and tampering with a witness, victim, or informant. Two accomplices, both 16, each face first-degree murder, principal in the first degree, and attempted armed robbery charges.One suspect was arrested in Jacksonville while two were taken into custody in Riviera Beach. Two of the three juveniles were previously known to law enforcement and had been in the system for several years, Coleman said.Advanced surveillance technology proved crucial in solving the case. Detectives used Flock camera and License Plate Reader technology to track the suspect vehicle as it fled the scene immediately after the shooting, following it to the suspects' homes.Coleman added that the department will continue using Flock cameras despite recent state restrictions on their use on state roads."We'll continue to use the Flock cameras until they go away, until the city leadership decide they don't no longer want them in the city," Coleman said. "They're invaluable to our investigation, how we use them."Coleman emphasized that the investigation remains active and additional arrests may be forthcoming. He also addressed the broader issue of youth violence plaguing the community."We've experienced a lot of activity like this in our community for many, many years, and we're starting to move forward, not just in this community, throughout Palm Beach County to plan together to address youth violence," Coleman said. Pastor Tony Drayton, a community leader who has worked for years to address violence in the area, joined Coleman at the press conference. "Our community has been bruised. Our community has been damaged," Drayton said. "And I do believe that just because we're bruised and damaged doesn't mean that we're at the point of failure. There's still hope."The three juveniles are being held at the Juvenile Assessment Center and have not been charged as adults. Coleman said the legal process will determine if they should be tried as adults based on state statutes.Coleman stressed that despite this incident, Riviera Beach remains a safe place to visit and live. "This is not a black eye or blemish on what all the great work we have done in this city," Coleman said. "Riviera Beach is a place that I consider a great place, and I want everybody outside of Riviera Beach to feel it's a great place to come and enjoy the beaches that we have and our communities."The investigation remains active. Anyone with additional information is urged to contact the Riviera Beach Police Department at 561-845-4123 or submit an anonymous tip through Crime Stoppers at 1-800-458-TIPS (8477).

entry.title: Florida's left-lane law has drivers guessing — here's what you need to know
entry.summary: Many Florida drivers may not know it is illegal to use the far-left lane as a general travel lane and a viewer's frustration sparked a test of just how well people know the law. Kevin Eddy drives from Stuart to Palm Beach County every day and said left-lane drivers are causing unwanted congestion on the roads. His concern prompted a closer look at what Florida law actually requires. Florida law requires drivers to use the far-left lane mainly for passing and not as a general travel lane. The rule applies to roads with a speed limit of 65 mph or higher. WATCH BELOW: Florida's left-lane law has drivers guessing here's what you need to know Testing drivers' knowledge about traveling in the left lane When asked whether they knew it was illegal to drive in the left lane, some drivers admitted they did not. 'I did not know,' Alfredo Milian said. 'I call it a gray area, but yes,' another driver said. 'I've heard about it, that it's illegal to. Or you're not supposed to drive in the left lane for a long period of time, always driving the right lane,' a third driver said. Eddy said better signage and stronger enforcement could help. 'You really don't have hardly any signs at all,' Eddy said. 'And you also have to realize we have a lot of tourists here, so we have a lot of people that aren't familiar with the laws in Florida,' Eddy said. There are exceptions to the left-lane rule during heavy traffic congestion, but experts say drivers should always merge back to the right after passing another car. entry.summary: Man shot outside Port St. Lucie Pollo Tropical now faces charges, police say    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 37-year-old man who was shot during a confrontation outside a Pollo Tropical in Port St. Lucie is now facing charges after investigators determined he was the primary aggressor in the encounter, according to police. Lucie Police Department said officers responded around 3:43 p.m. 19, to the restaurant at 1365 NW St. Lucie West Boulevard after receiving reports of a shooting. When officers arrived, they found Christopher Harris, 37, suffering from a gunshot wound to his upper torso. He was flown to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where his injuries were determined to be non-life-threatening, police said. The other person involved, identified by police as Isaiah Davis, 25, was detained at the scene while detectives investigated. Officers also recovered a firearm. According to investigators, the encounter began after Harris and Davis had an interaction in the restaurant's parking lot. Police said surveillance video showed Davis entering the restaurant to pick up a food delivery order and Harris following him inside, despite Harris not appearing to place or pick up an order. Police said Harris then followed Davis back outside, where exterior surveillance video showed Harris pushing Davis and advancing toward him as Davis moved backward. Investigators said Harris was armed with a knife during the confrontation, and witnesses reported seeing him with a knife shortly before the shooting. Davis fired one round, striking Harris in the chest, according to police. Harris went back inside the restaurant, where people began providing aid and called 911. Investigators said one knife was recovered after it had been removed from Harris' waistband while people were helping him. Police said another knife was later found in his front pocket. After reviewing surveillance video, physical evidence and witness statements, detectives determined Harris was the primary aggressor and established probable cause to charge him with attempted aggravated battery with a deadly weapon and felony battery based on a prior battery conviction, according to the department. Because Harris remained hospitalized, police said an arrest affidavit was submitted to the St. He is expected to be booked into the jail after he is medically released. Police said no criminal charges are currently pending against Davis. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates

entry.title: Molly's House marks 30 years of helping Treasure Coast families during medical treatment
entry.summary: Mollys House in Stuart is celebrating 30 years of providing affordable lodging and support services for patients and families receiving medical treatment on the Treasure Coast. The nonprofit organization, located in Stuart's medical district, was founded to help families stay close to doctors, hospitals and treatment providers during difficult medical situations. Leaders with Molly's House said the mission continues to focus on reducing stress for families facing long-term care and recovery. WATCH BELOW: Mollys House celebrates 30 years in Stuart Mollys House celebrates 30 years of helping families in Stuart Kate Wiegerink, a member of the Mollys House board of directors and Molly Sharkey's sister, said the organization also works to educate new doctors, nurses and community members about the services available to patients and families. 'We want people to know these resources exist,' Wiegerink said during the anniversary celebration. Molly's House provides affordable lodging for guests traveling for treatment and also offers a free cancer support program for residents, according to organization leaders. The nonprofit is celebrating the milestone with an open house Monday at its facility on Osceola Street in Stuart. Community members are invited to tour the house and healing garden while learning more about the organizations history and programs. Brandi Patricio, whose son TJ (Timothy) is receiving treatment, shared how the nonprofit has helped her family manage the financial and emotional challenges tied to ongoing medical care. Patricio said having access to affordable lodging reduces anxiety about housing costs during treatment and allows families to focus on recovery and care. In addition to housing support, Molly's House provides weekly free meals to residents to help ease food expenses and preparation during stressful medical situations. Businesses and individuals can become a 'Chef for a Day' and provide an average of 28 meals. The organizations leaders said demand for support services remains strong as more families seek affordable options near treatment centers across South Florida and the Treasure Coast.

entry.title: Stafford passes Philip Rivers on all-time TD list in Rams win
entry.summary: The Los Angeles Rams' dismal season opener in Australia and their proliferating injury woes were nothing Davante Adams and Matthew Stafford couldn't overcome back home with a vintage performance against the Giants. And after New York lost Jaxson Dart on the opening drive, it didn't stand a chance. Adams made eight catches for 195 yards and hauled in two of Staffords four touchdown passes, and the Rams welcomed Aaron Donald back to the NFL with a 28-6 victory Monday night. RELATED STORY | NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell agrees on a 4-year contract extension Stafford passed for 327 yards for the Rams (1-1), who capitalized after the Giants (1-1) lost Dart to a left knee injury on their seventh snap. Los Angeles outgained New York with 481 yards to 182, even overcoming two turnovers in a swagger-restoring blowout. This team, we got to the confidence level that we're at because of the work we put in, and we're not going to put any governors on what we can do here, said Adams, who had the fourth-highest yardage total of his 13-year career. If you're trying to be great, be a Super Bowl-caliber team, you've got to hold yourself to a high standard. We can do even a little bit better than what we did, but this is on track with what we're capable of. The Rams played without injured All-Pros Puka Nacua and Myles Garrett, but Stafford and Adams were in top form while the preseason Super Bowl favorites rebounded competently from last weeks 27-7 debacle of a Week 1 loss to the 49ers. Adams catches and yards receiving were both his best performances in a Rams uniform, while league MVP Stafford moved into sixth in NFL history with his 426th career TD pass, topping Philip Rivers when Adams adroitly tracked down an 11-yard fade in the third quarter. Adams was extraordinary in the second game of his 13th NFL season. He made a two-handed grab high above his head before taking it for a 31-yard touchdown on the Rams second possession, and he made a 64-yard catch on their third drive to set up Kyren Williams 10-yard TD catch. (Adams) was special, and it showed all night, coach Sean McVay said. I thought he made some great plays, but you can see there's a lot of trust he and Matthew have. It's only going to continue to build, and I was really happy for him. entry.summary: Much of this season for the Miami Dolphins will be about small victories even if actual wins are hard to come by. Miami stayed close to the San Francisco 49ers for the first half on Sunday. But contending for four quarters with a star-studded roster featuring All-Pros like Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle and Nick Bosa was too hard a task for the young Dolphins. 'Richard Raczkoski, beloved son, corporal, sheriff's department, Indian River County,' reads Marc Raczkoski, blinking back tears. It's the grave of his older brother, who was just 29 years old when he was buried at the Fort Pierce cemetery. 'I was 22,' Marc said quietly. 'I was 22.' It's always been an agonizing place for Marc one that's brought up too many painful memories. Yet this time, his grief feels a little lighter. This time, for the first time in the 40 years he's come to visit his older brother, he finally has the answer he's been longing to give. 'That I love him. And it's finally over,' Marc said. Friday, Governor Ron DeSantis signed the death warrant for William Reaves, the man convicted of killing Raczkoski in 1986. If carried out, the execution will mark Florida's 18th this year. It is scheduled for October 20, and Reaves has one last chance at an appeal. 'It gives closure,' Marc said. 'Now, when everybody asks me, 'What happened to the guy that murdered my brother?' That the first question I get, and I got to say, 'He's still still hasn't happened.' 'You'll finally have a different answer,' Investigative Reporter Kate Hussey supplied. 'Yes, finally have a different answer,' Marc replied. The shooting On September 23, 1986, 29-year-old Deputy Richard Raczkoski answered a 911 call at a convenience store in Indian River County. Minutes later, he was shot 4 times and killed, launching a multi-agency manhunt for the killer. Days later, authorities arrested 37-year-old William Reaves in Albany, Georgia, who was extradited back to Indian River County, where he confessed to killing Raczkoski, saying he 'panicked' when a gun fell out of his shorts, and that he was under the influence of drugs at the time. Forty years later, Marc said the memories of that night are still fresh and painful, recalling the middle-of-the-night knock on the door that changed everything. entry.title: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library helping boost early literacy in Palm Beach County and around the world
entry.summary: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library is making a difference for young readers around the world, and a completed international study is putting hard numbers behind the program's impact including right here in Palm Beach County. According to the 2025 Florida Assessment of Student Thinking (FAST) exams, 40 percent of third graders in Palm Beach County read below grade level. The Imagination Library says the program is helping close that gap. WATCH BELOW: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library boosts literacy worldwide Dolly Parton's Imagination Library boosts literacy worldwide WPTV reporter Christy Waite connected with Roxanne Mutchler, a board member with Palm Beach County's Imagination Library, who says an international study shows the impact the program is having globally. More than 86,000 people in five countries participated in the study. Some of the key findings that researchers found include: Compared to children who are not in the program, reading just 10 books gave children a clear head start in building vocabulary and learning to hear distinct sounds in words Children enrolled in the program are nine times more likely to have a book read to them four times a week Children in the U.S. program are also 11 times more likely to be interested in books '(Dolly Parton's) legacy lives on,' Mutchler said. Since being founded in Palm Beach County in 2000, the program has shipped out more than 40,000 books to local children. Parent Monique Boothe signed her four kids up about a year ago and it has allowed her kids to develop a love of reading starting at an early age. 'We want to get them off social media to build their vocabulary and imagination,' Boothe said. The Imagination Library is now seeing record-breaking enrollment numbers locally, with more than 200 children registered since Parton's death. Mutchler said the surge in interest has strained the program's website. 'We are experiencing a lot of traffic on the website, so if you have any trouble registering, just wait a few minutes and try again,' Mutchler said.

entry.title: Another Martin County High School threat sparks investigation, student arrested - cw34.com
entry.summary: Another Martin County High School threat sparks investigation, student arrested    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A 15-year-old student was arrested Tuesday after threatening Martin County High School , according to the district. Noah Taylor, a sophomore at the school, was arrested and charged with making a false report concerning the planting of a bomb, a second-degree felony. The threat was quickly determined to be a hoax, and students and staff remained safe throughout the investigation, according to the school district. Investigators with the Martin County Sheriff's Office said school resource officers and Criminal Investigations Division detectives traced the message back to Taylor. During the investigation, Taylor confessed to sending the threat, according to the Sheriff's Office. See also: Boynton woman accused of stealing $4,300 in skip-scan theft scheme that cost BJ's $18,000 The threat was reported through FortifyFL, Principal Lori Vogel previously told families. The Sheriff's Office immediately began investigating and identified the apparent source of the message. The district notified families Tuesday that an arrest had been made after initially telling parents an arrest appeared imminent. The Sheriff's Office said the arrest comes after multiple hoax bomb threats involving schools in the area in recent weeks. Investigators said they can only link Taylor to this specific threat. School officials said students found to have been involved in making threats could face both school disciplinary action and legal consequences. The district also reminded families that FortifyFL is an important tool for reporting legitimate safety concerns, but knowingly submitting false information or making a false threat can have serious consequences. False threats are neither harmless nor funny, Vogel said, adding that they can cause fear, disrupt learning, and place a burden on students, families, school employees, and law enforcement. The Sheriff's Office said threats made anonymously, through text messages, online, or through other electronic communications, can still be traced and investigated.
