entry.title: 'Not knowing where he is': Family searches for missing Port St. Lucie father - WPEC
entry.summary: 'Not knowing where he is': Family searches for missing Port St. Lucie father    WPEC
entry.article_text: Eight months after a Port St. Lucie father vanished, his family says they are still searching for answers and living with the painful uncertainty of not knowing where he is. "I'm stuck in this cycle of not knowing where he is," said Aubrey Finley, whose brother, Robert La Polla , disappeared Jan. 8 after being released from a hospital in Fort Pierce. The 47-year-old father has not been seen or heard from since, according to his family. Detectives have no confirmed sightings, and the case remains unsolved. Finley said La Polla struggled with depression following the deaths of their parents, but the siblings remained close and talked often. "Everything kind of fell apart," she said. "But we still managed to communicate a lot. We were still there for each other all the time." Also read: Search underway for missing autistic man last seen at Jensen Beach home Thursday morning Because of that bond, Finley said her brother's disappearance is completely out of character. In the months since he vanished, family members and friends have organized search efforts across Fort Pierce, checking wooded areas and busy corridors near HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. "We've gone through woods, under bridges, talking to people everywhere in Fort Pierce, trying to find anything that brings us to him," Finley said. The search has also taken an emotional toll on La Polla's young daughter, who continues to wait for her father to come home. She misses him," Finley said. "He's got a family that love him." The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office (SLCSO) said La Polla has been entered into a national missing persons database. Investigators have also collected DNA from family members in case it is needed for identification and continue to follow up on leads. Anyone with information about La Polla's whereabouts is asked to contact Detective Cpl. Drawdy at 772-462-3230 or call 911.

entry.summary: King tides, full moon erode Fort Pierce road for second time in a week    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Crews returned to South Indian River Drive in Fort Pierce on Wednesday to repair a washed-out embankment for the second time in a week, as king tides and recent rain continue to affect parts of South Florida. Skid loaders were working along the narrow roadway beside the Indian River Lagoon, adding dirt and sand to reinforce an area where erosion has left the road’s edge vulnerable. Crews brought 32 loads of dirt to the site Sept. But only days later, the embankment again needed repairs. Resident Gene Barnes said the recurring work is not a long-term solution. We’re losing ground year by year, Barnes said. Until the Corps of Engineers or something like that comes and puts a headwall in to stabilize it, it’s not going to be an easy fix. The road has faced erosion problems before. Heavy rain damaged sections in 2014, and Hurricane Nicole caused additional washouts in 2022. Barnes said continued rain and tidal action could undermine the roadway itself. See also: Case reopened: Port St. Lucie TikTok creator jailed on computer-access charge If we keep getting rains like this, it’s going to undermine the road, and then the road is going to collapse and the school bus is going to fall in the hole, he said. The latest repairs follow an emergency sand operation at nearby Jetty Park that cost taxpayers nearly $500,000. While repairs on South Indian River Drive may be less costly, residents said the erosion is likely to remain a concern as more rain and tidal action are forecast.

entry.title: Rabies alert issued in Martin County after raccoon tests positive in Stuart - WPEC
entry.summary: Rabies alert issued in Martin County after raccoon tests positive in Stuart    WPEC
entry.article_text: A rabid raccoon found in Stuart prompted the Florida Department of Health in Martin County to issue a 60-day alert Wednesday. The raccoon was captured Sunday off South Kanner Highway and later tested positive for rabies , according to the department. The alert covered an area bounded by Southeast Tressler Drive to the south, Southeast Federal Highway to the east and South Kanner Highway to the west. Health officials said rabies was present among wild animals in the area and urged residents and visitors to avoid contact with raccoons, bats, foxes, skunks, otters, bobcats, coyotes and other wildlife. Rabies is a deadly viral disease most commonly transmitted through the bite or scratch of an infected animal. An animal with rabies may appear healthy and can behave unusually friendly or aggressively. People who are bitten or scratched by a wild or domestic animal should wash the wound with soap and water, seek medical attention and report the incident to the Department of Health in Martin County at 772-221-4030 . Treatment administered after an exposure can prevent the disease. Officials recommended that residents take several precautions: Keep pets and livestock current on rabies vaccinations. Keep pets leashed and under direct supervision. Avoid handling or feeding wild and stray animals. Do not leave pet food or unsecured garbage outdoors. Prevent bats and other wildlife from entering homes, schools and other occupied buildings. Contact a licensed wildlife rehabilitator rather than bringing a wild animal into a home. See also: Florida mother leaves 4 children home alone while on Carnival cruise to Bahamas: Police Anyone whose pet or livestock is bitten should immediately contact a veterinarian and Martin County Animal Control at 772-463-3211 . Residents can also call animal control to report stray animals in their neighborhoods. More information is available at FloridaHealth.gov/Rabies .

entry.article_text: The trial of former Fort Pierce City Manager Nicholas Mimms, who faces accusations of bid tampering and official misconduct, continued with testimony from his niece and a lead investigator. The first witness called to the stand was one of the lead investigators in the case, and cross-examination became tense at times. The prosecution’s key witness was Mimms’ niece, Caleta Scott, who is one of the founders of the nonprofit Lincoln Park Young Professionals. Mimms was my uncle when I applied," Scott said during her testimony. When asked about her relationship with Mimms, Scott said, "I respected him in the role of city manager and called him Mr. Mimms." Mimms is accused of using his position to help Lincoln Park Young Professionals secure a lease to develop two city-owned properties. The prosecution argues that Scott received special treatment because of her relationship with Mimms, presenting it as a conflict of interest. The defense has previously argued that Mimms and Scott have a distant relationship and that Mimms did not conspire to commit the alleged crimes. Testimony also included statements from the lead investigator in the case for the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, with cross-examination becoming tense at times. entry.title: St. Lucie County Fire District attorney gives 90-day notice amid firefighter hazing fight - WPEC
entry.summary: St. Lucie County Fire District attorney gives 90-day notice amid firefighter hazing fight    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie County Fire District Attorney Kim Sabol is leaving the department, submitting her 90-day notice Wednesday as the agency faces an ongoing fight with its firefighters' union over the termination of three employees accused of hazing rookies. Sabol confirmed she submitted her notice Wednesday. It was not immediately clear whether her departure is connected to the ongoing dispute. My employment agreement requires 90 days' notice because it's a 3-year contract," Sabol told CBS12. "My last work day will be 12/31/2026." Sabol has served as the district's attorney since 2017, advising the Fire Board, fire chief and administration on legal matters including labor and employment issues and collective bargaining. Her departure comes as Professional Firefighters and Paramedics of St. Lucie County Local 1377 fights the discipline of five firefighters. The union has formally demanded arbitration for three terminated firefighters and two suspended personnel, arguing there was no just cause for the discipline. See also: Beyond the dashcam: FHP begins equipping troopers with body cameras The firefighters were disciplined after an outside investigation into videos showing senior personnel using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to newer firefighters in incidents in March and September 2024. Fire District officials called the conduct hazing and said it violated department policies and created a culture of intimidation between senior and junior employees. According to previous reports , Local 1377 President Ryan Sapp said the incidents amounted to consensual station horseplay, pointing to an earlier Fort Pierce Police Department investigation that found no criminal wrongdoing. There was no kind of hazing whatsoever, and I could not believe that that's what was found," Sapp told CBS12. The union has also challenged the fairness of the Fire District's investigation, which was conducted by outside attorney John "J.K." Keller IV. Sapp said union attorneys believe the investigation was not impartial and that some questions appeared to be designed to reach a predetermined conclusion. The union also raised concerns that the law firm involved in the investigation has since been retained by the district for the upcoming arbitration. Two terminated firefighters, Jordon Hutchinson and Christopher Baldwin, have separately alleged whistleblower retaliation. Lucie County Fire District received a 90-day notice of a resignation from its legal counsel today. The District Attorney is eligible for retirement, and the notice provides for continued service during the 90-day period," St. Lucie County Fire Rescue said in a statement. "The District will not speculate regarding the circumstances surrounding the resignation or any connection to other matters. Sapp said the union remains willing to negotiate a resolution that could avoid arbitration, but any compromise would need to include reinstatement of the terminated firefighters. Sabol's 90-day notice means she is expected to remain with the district during that period unless the terms of her departure change.

entry.title: Case reopened: Port St. Lucie TikTok creator jailed on computer-access charge - WPEC
entry.summary: Case reopened: Port St. Lucie TikTok creator jailed on computer-access charge    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie man whose TikTok and Twich bios identify him as a cybersecurity engineer was jailed Wednesday after police reopened an investigation that had been closed in May. Mark Stephen Asea, 36, was booked into the St. Lucie County Jail on Sept. on one pending count of offense against computer users, according to jail records. His bond was set at $35,000. An earlier stalking charge appears to have been dropped. The charge stems from an earlier investigation in which detectives accused Asea of gaining access to women’s electronic devices and using TikTok posts to discuss information they said was private. In a warrant affidavit, a detective described reviewing videos from an account linked to Asea. The profile’s bio identifies its user as a narcissistic abuse survivor, former satanist, empath, cybersecurity engineer and woodsman. Police said one video included references to a woman’s password, device information, banking activity, license plate number and possible location tracking. The woman told investigators the password had been shared only in a closed TikTok group chat and that she had not given Asea permission to share it. Another woman told police Asea previously had remote access to her computer to help with an application. She became concerned, investigators said, after an image from a private Telegram message appeared in one of his TikTok posts. See also: Florida Education Department eyes dress code to ban head coverings, Crocs, short skirts The earlier affidavit alleged Asea posted more than 100 TikTok videos mentioning one of the women, including as many as six in a day. Detectives also cited videos that appeared to show computer equipment and coding as they investigated whether he had accessed devices without authorization. Asea’s booking photo shows him with long dark hair and prominent geometric tattoos across his face.

entry.title: Florida Election 2026: Voter Registration, Vote-by-Mail and Early Voting deadlines you need to know
entry.summary: Floridians who want to cast a ballot in the 2026 General Election have until Monday, Oct. 5, to register to vote or update their voter registration information. Voters are encouraged to verify that their registration details, including their name, address and party affiliation, are accurate before the deadline. Voters are also urged to confirm their Election Day polling location. Election Day is scheduled for Tuesday, Nov. 3, with polls open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Residents can register to vote or update their registration online through Florida's voter registration website , by mail or in person using a Florida Voter Registration Application. Applications are also available at Supervisor of Elections Offices and other designated voter registration agencies. Key election deadlines Voter registration deadline: Monday, Oct. 5, 2026 Vote-by-mail request deadline: Thursday, Oct. 22, 2026, by 5 p.m. Early voting dates, locations Palm Beach County: Oct. 19-Nov. 1 from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Voters can cast their ballot at any of the 28 locations during this time. Vote-by-mail return deadline is Nov. 3, 2026, by 7 p.m. at the Main Office or by 5 p.m. at a Branch Office or Secure Ballot Intake Station Martin County: Oct. 21-31 from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. each day at six locations across the county. St. Lucie County: Oct. 1931 from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily, including Sunday, Oct. 25. The county will have eight early-voting locations across the county. Indian River County: Oct. 19-31 from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. with extended hours on Thursdays from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Four early-voting locations will be available throughout the county. Vote-by-mail ballots must be received by the Supervisor of Elections office by 7 p.m. Election Day to be counted and may be returned to a secure ballot intake station located at each early voting location during early voting hours, or in person to the Supervisor of Elections office. Okeechobee County: Oct. 24-31 from 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. at one location: 307 NW 5th Avenue in Okeechobee Election Day: Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026, from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Voters must cast their ballot at their assigned precinct.

entry.title: From heartbreak to hope: Jupiter mother turns personal loss into community support
entry.summary: After years of infertility, pregnancy loss and unanswered questions, one Jupiter mother is turning her personal journey into a source of hope for others. The inaugural Hope Rising 5K and Fun Walk will take place Oct. 17 at Carlin Park, bringing together families, wellness providers and community partners with a shared goal: ensuring that no one facing infertility or pregnancy loss feels alone. WATCH: Jupiter woman creates Hope Rising after infertility journey Jupiter mom turns pregnancy loss into hope for other families For founder Kimberly Malik, the event grew from her own experience navigating five miscarriages and four years of infertility. 'When you get told unexplained infertility, that's not really what you want to hear and that's not an answer I can accept,' Malik said. She spent years researching, advocating for herself and searching for answers before ultimately learning she had a blood-clotting condition that contributed to her losses. Despite the heartbreak, Malik said the experience eventually led her to a larger purpose. 'Welcomed our rainbow baby on Nov. 8 of 2024, my husband's birthday, and I just felt this calling of don't let others walk alone,' she said. That mission became the foundation of Hope Rising. Building a community of support Malik says one of the most difficult parts of infertility and pregnancy loss is the isolation many families experience. The Hope Rising event is designed to change that. Organizers are bringing together local businesses, wellness providers and community partners to create a Support Village where attendees can connect with resources and others who understand the journey firsthand. 'We can have those that unfortunately are on a fertility journey feel seen and supported,' Malik said. Among those helping organize the event is Jenny Frattaruolo, owner of Jupiter Fit Club, who became part of Malik's support system during her fertility journey. 'Just having resources and having someone along the journey with you is everything,' Malik said during an earlier interview. More than a race While the event centers around a 5K and fun walk, organizers say the focus extends far beyond race day. entry.title: Toddler drowns in pond near family home in Martin County - cw34.com
entry.summary: Toddler drowns in pond near family home in Martin County    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A 23-month-old boy died Tuesday evening after he was found in a pond on his family's property, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office . Deputies identified the child as Pablo Mendoza-Arroyo, who is remembered by loved ones for his bright smile and joyful spirit. Investigators say Pablo was outside with family members in the yard of a home along Darling Street in Port Salerno shortly after 5 p.m. Tuesday when he went out of sight. His mother and aunt realized he was missing and began searching. They later found him in a pond on the property Sheriff John Budensiek said the father was mowing the yard while the mother and her sister played with other children. Budensiek said there had been a fence around the pond at one point, but it had broken down over time and was no longer working. "It's a pond where if you walk in two feet, it drops off. And if you don't know how to swim, you're going to be in trouble," Budensiek said. "And in this case, sadly, our two-year-old did not know how to swim." Family members took the child to Cleveland Clinic South Hospital. The sheriff's office said he was pronounced dead in the emergency room despite lifesaving efforts. See also: Florida mother leaves 4 children home alone while on Carnival cruise to Bahamas: Police Family members told investigators the boy was out of sight for no more than 10 minutes, according to the sheriff's office. MCSO criminal investigators interviewed everyone at the scene and are reviewing the circumstances of the child's death. Budensiek said Wednesday that the medical examiner ruled the death an accidental drowning after an autopsy. "From all indications, everything that we've got through our investigation, this is a tragic accident," Budensiek said. One relative, Virginia Maldonado, said she hopes people remember Pablo by his smile and keep the family in their prayers. Others told CBS12 News Pablo was deeply loved by a large extended family spanning beyond Florida. According to the sheriff, investigators found no signs that the parents were reckless or inattentive. "Parents get distracted, I know that. So no one is disparaging the parents. In this case, this was an accidental drowning," Budensiek said. Budensiek encouraged parents to get young children into swim lessons and said the YMCA offers free classes for children as young as 2. Mindy York, president and co-founder of Baby Otter Swim School, said supervision is the most important way to prevent drownings. She also recommended door alarms, locked pool gates, and CPR training for parents. She said teaching children to swim is just as important. "We want to make sure that a child knows what to do if they fall into a body of water. Teach your children how to swim. It's like here in Florida, right? It's the leading cause of death in children under the age of five. With this death, now we're at 99," York said. She said children are never too young to start swim lessons. "I'm telling you, they absorb everything. So, we start at nine months, and we. We go all the way up to adults. So they're not too young to learn anything. They understand everything you say. And with a proper technique and speaking to them, they get it," York said. A GoFundMe has been established to help Pablo Mendoza-Arroyo's family with expenses following his tragic death. Those who would like to support the family can donate here .

entry.title: Rabies alert issued in Indian River County after rabid bat found near apartment complex
entry.summary: The Florida Department of Health in Indian River County has issued a 60-day rabies alert after a bat captured near the Sonrise Apartments tested positive for the virus. Health officials said the bat was captured in the Sonrise Apartments area off Sonrise Place in Fellsmere on Sept. 24. Anyone who may have had contact with or touched the bat is urged to contact the Department of Health in Indian River County at 772-794-7472. The alert comes as health officials monitor rabies activity among wild animals in the area and warn residents that the disease is present in the local wildlife population. Rabies is a viral disease that affects the nervous system of mammals, including humans. Health officials say people who are exposed to rabies can protect themselves by seeking prompt medical treatment after exposure. The Department of Health is reminding residents and visitors to avoid contact with wild animals such as raccoons, bats, foxes, skunks, otters, bobcats and coyotes, which are more likely to carry the disease. Officials also recommend taking several precautions to reduce the risk of exposure, including: Keeping pets vaccinated against rabies Supervising pets and keeping them on a leash Securing livestock on private property Avoiding contact with wild or stray animals, including cats Not feeding or handling wildlife Preventing bats and other wildlife from entering homes, schools and other occupied buildings Anyone bitten or scratched by a wild or domestic animal should seek medical attention and report the incident to the Department of Health in Indian River County at 772-794-7472. If a pet or livestock animal is bitten by another animal, owners should contact a veterinarian immediately and notify Indian River County Animal Control at 772-226-4799. Visit the Florida Department of Health website for more information on rabies.

entry.title: Case reopened: Port St. Lucie TikTok creator jailed on computer-access charge - cw34.com
entry.summary: Case reopened: Port St. Lucie TikTok creator jailed on computer-access charge    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Lucie man whose TikTok and Twich bios identify him as a cybersecurity engineer was jailed Wednesday after police reopened an investigation that had been closed in May. Mark Stephen Asea, 36, was booked into the St. Lucie County Jail on Sept. on one pending count of offense against computer users, according to jail records. His bond was set at $35,000. An earlier stalking charge appears to have been dropped. The charge stems from an earlier investigation in which detectives accused Asea of gaining access to women’s electronic devices and using TikTok posts to discuss information they said was private. In a warrant affidavit, a detective described reviewing videos from an account linked to Asea. The profile’s bio identifies its user as a narcissistic abuse survivor, former satanist, empath, cybersecurity engineer and woodsman. Police said one video included references to a woman’s password, device information, banking activity, license plate number and possible location tracking. The woman told investigators the password had been shared only in a closed TikTok group chat and that she had not given Asea permission to share it. Another woman told police Asea previously had remote access to her computer to help with an application. She became concerned, investigators said, after an image from a private Telegram message appeared in one of his TikTok posts. See also: Florida Education Department eyes dress code to ban head coverings, Crocs, short skirts The earlier affidavit alleged Asea posted more than 100 TikTok videos mentioning one of the women, including as many as six in a day. Detectives also cited videos that appeared to show computer equipment and coding as they investigated whether he had accessed devices without authorization. Asea’s booking photo shows him with long dark hair and prominent geometric tattoos across his face.

entry.title: Toddler drowns in pond near family home in Martin County - WPEC
entry.summary: Toddler drowns in pond near family home in Martin County    WPEC
entry.article_text: A 23-month-old boy died Tuesday evening after he was found in a pond on his family's property, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office . Deputies identified the child as Pablo Mendoza-Arroyo, who is remembered by loved ones for his bright smile and joyful spirit. Investigators say Pablo was outside with family members in the yard of a home along Darling Street in Port Salerno shortly after 5 p.m. Tuesday when he went out of sight. His mother and aunt realized he was missing and began searching. They later found him in a pond on the property Sheriff John Budensiek said the father was mowing the yard while the mother and her sister played with other children. Budensiek said there had been a fence around the pond at one point, but it had broken down over time and was no longer working. "It's a pond where if you walk in two feet, it drops off. And if you don't know how to swim, you're going to be in trouble," Budensiek said. "And in this case, sadly, our two-year-old did not know how to swim." Family members took the child to Cleveland Clinic South Hospital. The sheriff's office said he was pronounced dead in the emergency room despite lifesaving efforts. See also: Florida mother leaves 4 children home alone while on Carnival cruise to Bahamas: Police Family members told investigators the boy was out of sight for no more than 10 minutes, according to the sheriff's office. MCSO criminal investigators interviewed everyone at the scene and are reviewing the circumstances of the child's death. Budensiek said Wednesday that the medical examiner ruled the death an accidental drowning after an autopsy. "From all indications, everything that we've got through our investigation, this is a tragic accident," Budensiek said. One relative, Virginia Maldonado, said she hopes people remember Pablo by his smile and keep the family in their prayers. Others told CBS12 News Pablo was deeply loved by a large extended family spanning beyond Florida. According to the sheriff, investigators found no signs that the parents were reckless or inattentive. "Parents get distracted, I know that. So no one is disparaging the parents. In this case, this was an accidental drowning," Budensiek said. Budensiek encouraged parents to get young children into swim lessons and said the YMCA offers free classes for children as young as 2. Mindy York, president and co-founder of Baby Otter Swim School, said supervision is the most important way to prevent drownings. She also recommended door alarms, locked pool gates, and CPR training for parents. She said teaching children to swim is just as important. "We want to make sure that a child knows what to do if they fall into a body of water. Teach your children how to swim. It's like here in Florida, right? It's the leading cause of death in children under the age of five. With this death, now we're at 99," York said. She said children are never too young to start swim lessons. "I'm telling you, they absorb everything. So, we start at nine months, and we. We go all the way up to adults. So they're not too young to learn anything. They understand everything you say. And with a proper technique and speaking to them, they get it," York said. A GoFundMe has been established to help Pablo Mendoza-Arroyo's family with expenses following his tragic death. Those who would like to support the family can donate here .

entry.title: Florida Election 2026: Voter Registration, Vote-by-Mail and Early Voting deadlines you need to know
entry.summary: Floridians who want to cast a ballot in the 2026 General Election have until Monday, Oct. 5, to register to vote or update their voter registration information. Voters are encouraged to verify that their registration details, including their name, address and party affiliation, are accurate before the deadline. Voters are also urged to confirm their Election Day polling location. Election Day is scheduled for Tuesday, Nov. 3, with polls open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Residents can register to vote or update their registration online through Florida's voter registration website , by mail or in person using a Florida Voter Registration Application. Applications are also available at Supervisor of Elections Offices and other designated voter registration agencies. Key election deadlines Voter registration deadline: Monday, Oct. 5, 2026 Vote-by-mail request deadline: Thursday, Oct. 22, 2026, by 5 p.m. Early voting dates, locations Palm Beach County: Oct. 19-Nov. 1 from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Voters can cast their ballot at any of the 28 locations during this time. Vote-by-mail return deadline is Nov. 3, 2026, by 7 p.m. at the Main Office or by 5 p.m. at a Branch Office or Secure Ballot Intake Station Martin County: Oct. 21-31 from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. each day at six locations across the county. St. Lucie County: Oct. 1931 from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily, including Sunday, Oct. 25. The county will have eight early-voting locations across the county. Indian River County: Oct. 19-31 from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. with extended hours on Thursdays from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Four early-voting locations will be available throughout the county. Vote-by-mail ballots must be received by the Supervisor of Elections office by 7 p.m. Election Day to be counted and may be returned to a secure ballot intake station located at each early voting location during early voting hours, or in person to the Supervisor of Elections office. Okeechobee County: Oct. 24-31 from 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. at one location: 307 NW 5th Avenue in Okeechobee Election Day: Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026, from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Voters must cast their ballot at their assigned precinct.

entry.title: Panthers captain Aleksander Barkov leaves against Sharks because of apparent knee injury
entry.summary: Florida captain Aleksander Barkov left in the second period of the Panthers' 4-3 overtime loss to San Jose on Thursday night after his left knee appeared to buckle during a scrum with Sharks defender Darnell Nurse and forward Zack Ostapchuk along the boards. Barkov immediately left the ice, throwing his glove on the ground as he headed into the tunnel. RELATED: More Panthers news After the game, Florida coach Paul Maurice did not specify the type of injury Barkov suffered, but said the team would know the extent of the severity Friday. 'It's not related to his injury last year at all,' Maurice said. 'We'll have a good idea by tomorrow afternoon.' Barkov missed all of last season after tearing his right ACL and MCL during training camp. The 31-year-old Finn was playing his second game this season. Luca Cagnoni scores in OT in the Sharks' season-opening victory over the Panthers Luca Cagnoni rocketed a shot off goalie Akira Schmid at 3:14 of overtime and the San Jose Sharks opened the season with a 4-3 victory over the Florida Panthers on Thursday night. Florida overcame a three-goal deficit to force overtime, with Eetu Luostarinen scoring twice and Matthew Tkachuk pulling the Panthers even at 5:18 of the third. Luostarinen and Tkachuk scored in a 17-second span. Mason Marchment opened the scoring for San Jose with 5:40 to go in the first period. Will Smith scored twice in the second period, the first short-handed and the second on a power play, both off assists from Macklin Celebrini. Smith and Celebrini each had three-point nights. Sharks goalie Yaroslav Askarov made 23 saves. Schmid stopped 28 shots. Multiple scuffles broke out throughout the game, highlighted by Tkachuk and Jacob Trouba squaring off in the center of the rink. The Panthers will head south and play Anaheim on Sunday night.

entry.summary: King tides, full moon erode Fort Pierce road for second time in a week    WPEC
entry.article_text: Crews returned to South Indian River Drive in Fort Pierce on Wednesday to repair a washed-out embankment for the second time in a week, as king tides and recent rain continue to affect parts of South Florida. Skid loaders were working along the narrow roadway beside the Indian River Lagoon, adding dirt and sand to reinforce an area where erosion has left the road’s edge vulnerable. Crews brought 32 loads of dirt to the site Sept. But only days later, the embankment again needed repairs. Resident Gene Barnes said the recurring work is not a long-term solution. We’re losing ground year by year, Barnes said. Until the Corps of Engineers or something like that comes and puts a headwall in to stabilize it, it’s not going to be an easy fix. The road has faced erosion problems before. Heavy rain damaged sections in 2014, and Hurricane Nicole caused additional washouts in 2022. Barnes said continued rain and tidal action could undermine the roadway itself. See also: Case reopened: Port St. Lucie TikTok creator jailed on computer-access charge If we keep getting rains like this, it’s going to undermine the road, and then the road is going to collapse and the school bus is going to fall in the hole, he said. The latest repairs follow an emergency sand operation at nearby Jetty Park that cost taxpayers nearly $500,000. While repairs on South Indian River Drive may be less costly, residents said the erosion is likely to remain a concern as more rain and tidal action are forecast.

entry.article_text: The Florida Department of Health in Indian River County has issued a 60-day rabies alert after a bat captured near the Sonrise Apartments tested positive for the virus. Health officials said the bat was captured in the Sonrise Apartments area off Sonrise Place in Fellsmere on Sept. Anyone who may have had contact with or touched the bat is urged to contact the Department of Health in Indian River County at 772-794-7472. The alert comes as health officials monitor rabies activity among wild animals in the area and warn residents that the disease is present in the local wildlife population. Rabies is a viral disease that affects the nervous system of mammals, including humans. Health officials say people who are exposed to rabies can protect themselves by seeking prompt medical treatment after exposure. The Department of Health is reminding residents and visitors to avoid contact with wild animals such as raccoons, bats, foxes, skunks, otters, bobcats and coyotes, which are more likely to carry the disease. Officials also recommend taking several precautions to reduce the risk of exposure, including: Anyone bitten or scratched by a wild or domestic animal should seek medical attention and report the incident to the Department of Health in Indian River County at 772-794-7472. If a pet or livestock animal is bitten by another animal, owners should contact a veterinarian immediately and notify Indian River County Animal Control at 772-226-4799. Visit the Florida Department of Health website for more information on rabies.

entry.title: Case reopened: Port St. Lucie TikTok creator jailed on computer-access charge - cbs12.com
entry.summary: Case reopened: Port St. Lucie TikTok creator jailed on computer-access charge    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Lucie man whose TikTok and Twich bios identify him as a cybersecurity engineer was jailed Wednesday after police reopened an investigation that had been closed in May. Mark Stephen Asea, 36, was booked into the St. Lucie County Jail on Sept. on one pending count of offense against computer users, according to jail records. His bond was set at $35,000. An earlier stalking charge appears to have been dropped. The charge stems from an earlier investigation in which detectives accused Asea of gaining access to women’s electronic devices and using TikTok posts to discuss information they said was private. In a warrant affidavit, a detective described reviewing videos from an account linked to Asea. The profile’s bio identifies its user as a narcissistic abuse survivor, former satanist, empath, cybersecurity engineer and woodsman. Police said one video included references to a woman’s password, device information, banking activity, license plate number and possible location tracking. The woman told investigators the password had been shared only in a closed TikTok group chat and that she had not given Asea permission to share it. Another woman told police Asea previously had remote access to her computer to help with an application. She became concerned, investigators said, after an image from a private Telegram message appeared in one of his TikTok posts. See also: Florida Education Department eyes dress code to ban head coverings, Crocs, short skirts The earlier affidavit alleged Asea posted more than 100 TikTok videos mentioning one of the women, including as many as six in a day. Detectives also cited videos that appeared to show computer equipment and coding as they investigated whether he had accessed devices without authorization. Asea’s booking photo shows him with long dark hair and prominent geometric tattoos across his face.

entry.title: 'Not knowing where he is': Family searches for missing Port St. Lucie father - cbs12.com
entry.summary: 'Not knowing where he is': Family searches for missing Port St. Lucie father    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Eight months after a Port St. Lucie father vanished, his family says they are still searching for answers and living with the painful uncertainty of not knowing where he is. "I'm stuck in this cycle of not knowing where he is," said Aubrey Finley, whose brother, Robert La Polla , disappeared Jan. 8 after being released from a hospital in Fort Pierce. The 47-year-old father has not been seen or heard from since, according to his family. Detectives have no confirmed sightings, and the case remains unsolved. Finley said La Polla struggled with depression following the deaths of their parents, but the siblings remained close and talked often. "Everything kind of fell apart," she said. "But we still managed to communicate a lot. We were still there for each other all the time." Because of that bond, Finley said her brother's disappearance is completely out of character. In the months since he vanished, family members and friends have organized search efforts across Fort Pierce, checking wooded areas and busy corridors near HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. "We've gone through woods, under bridges, talking to people everywhere in Fort Pierce, trying to find anything that brings us to him," Finley said. The search has also taken an emotional toll on La Polla's young daughter, who continues to wait for her father to come home. She misses him," Finley said. "He's got a family that love him." The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office (SLCSO) said La Polla has been entered into a national missing persons database. Investigators have also collected DNA from family members in case it is needed for identification and continue to follow up on leads. Anyone with information about La Polla's whereabouts is asked to contact Detective Cpl. Drawdy at 772-462-3230 or call 911.

entry.title: Returning Stuart city manager Michael Mortell vows to improve city structure, restore public trust
entry.summary: Stuart's returning city manager says he has unfinished business and a plan to bring more structure to City Hall. Michael Mortell is back in his role as Stuart city manager. In his first interview since officially returning to the role Friday, Mortell told me he still has more to give the city. WATCH BELOW: Returning Stuart city manager vows to restore public trust Returning Stuart city manager Michael Mortell vows to improve city structure 'There's something drawing me. I feel the need to go back and finish the unwritten book or the unwritten chapter,' Mortell said. 'I felt like there was things that were left that needed to be corrected and needed to be finished.' After his dismissal last October, Mortell worked for the 19th Judicial Circuit, where he says he learned practices that could help the city run more efficiently. 'We need to really focus on defining administration defining whatwho are the policymakers, who the administrators, who is the chain of command, and how we need to disseminate information,' Mortell said. 'Implementing more structure and defining it will help all of us make the city a better place and I think residents will know exactly what to expect.' Over the past year, a divided Stuart Commission and leadership turnover have left some residents questioning their confidence in city government. Resident David Kelman voiced those concerns at a previous city commission meeting. 'You all represent this city. You need to step back and unite because what you're doing ain't going to work. It's three versus two here,' Kelman said. I asked Mortell how he plans to restore the community's faith in the city. He says it starts with teamwork. 'We really identify everybody's strengths ... and find ways to work more as a team so that everybody feels like they're contributing to the outcome and that everybody has the common goal of what's best for Stuart in mind and rather than being divisive at all to try to find ways to work together,' Mortell said. A city manager with a long history working for the city, Mortell is returning to the job with a fresh approach. entry.title: 'Who put it up?' Unpermitted license plate readers found in St. Lucie County
entry.summary: WPTV learned there are 13 license plate reader cameras in St. Lucie County that don't have permits, according to county staff. Wednesday, Sept. 30, was the deadline the Florida Department of Transportation gave municipalities to remove the license plate readers from state-controlled roads. WATCH BELOW: Unpermitted license plate readers found in St. Lucie County Unpermitted license plate readers found in St. Lucie County Now WPTV is pressing city leaders about why the cameras are there, who they belong to, and what is happening to the cameras now. On Thursday, WPTV spoke to Ricky Mathura, who works at a gas station off Orange Avenue and 25 th Street in Fort Pierce, where one of the unpermitted license plate readers was found. 'I don't know why it's there,' said Mathura. 'Who put it up?' St. Lucie County Communications Director Erick Gill said they're trying to find that out. 'We don't know who they belong to,' Gill said. 'They were just put in our right-of-way.' The county says there's 53 permitted license plate readers on their right-of-ways and gave WPTV a list with all the locations of the unpermitted license plate readers staff found. RELATED: FDOT revokes permits for automated license plate readers FDOT revokes permits for automated license plate readers 'We were surprised, you know, that were that many out there, said Gill. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office told WPTV they claimed three of them but are working to find out why they weren't permitted. Gill said county staff is actively working to identify the owners of the other readers and taped notices on the cameras for the owners to take them down within 30 days. Once the 30 days are up, Gill said staff will remove the readers safely. 'We'll begin the process of either removing them if we feel like we can safely remove them without damaging the equipment and endangering our staff, or at least covering up so the cameras can't capture any surveillance,' Gill said.

entry.title: Two men arrested in separate Port St. Lucie hit-and-run cases - cbs12.com
entry.summary: Two men arrested in separate Port St. Lucie hit-and-run cases    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Two men are out of jail on bond after being arrested in two separate hit-and-run cases in Port St. Lucie this week, according to the Port St. According to an arrest affidavit, 23-year-old Giovanny Barthelemy was driving a silver Toyota Highlander around 8:40 p.m. Tuesday when it collided with a 16-year-old riding an electric motorcycle on Southwest Roma Way near Southwest Lorenzo Way. A security camera at the community clubhouse recorded the crash. The officer wrote that the video shows the SUV turning into the community entrance as the teen crossed in front of it. The teen was thrown from the motorcycle. The affidavit says the SUV then backed up and drove away while the injured teen lay on the ground waving his arms. The teen was taken to Tradition Medical Center and then flown to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. Police said he broke his left femur and hurt his left ankle, and he was listed in serious but stable condition. See also: Rapper Rick Ross arrested in Florida on domestic violence charges, enters not guilty plea One witness told police the electric motorcycle had no headlights. Two witnesses said both vehicles were going fast. The SUV's owner, the father of Barthelemy's girlfriend, called 911. He told police Barthelemy said he had hit someone on a bike and then driven home. Officers found Barthelemy at his home on Southwest Ridgecrest Drive. According to the affidavit, after being read his rights, Barthelemy told police he felt and heard the crash and knew right away he had hit a person. He told police he should have stopped but didn't, and said his phone was dead, according to the affidavit. Barthelemy is charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving injuries, which is a felony. He was also given a traffic citation. He was released on a $7,500 bond. The second case happened earlier that afternoon. Lucie officer clocked a silver Toyota going 85 mph in a 40-mph zone, according to an arrest affidavit. The officer turned around and tried to stop the car. The affidavit says the driver went over a concrete median into the opposite lanes, ran a red light, and hit a traffic sign at Southwest Becker Road and Southwest Hallmark Street before getting on northbound Interstate 95. The officer turned off his lights and siren but kept the car in sight. Police said the car later broke down on the side of I-95. Officers said the driver, 19-year-old Christian Johnson, got out and ran toward the back of the car. Lucie detective, a Florida Highway Patrol trooper, and the officer surrounded the car, and Johnson was taken into custody. According to the affidavit, Johnson's license had been suspended three times in St. Johnson is charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving property damage, reckless driving and driving with a suspended or revoked license. All three charges are misdemeanors. He was released on a $12,500 bond. In a statement about both arrests, the Port St. Lucie Police Department said drivers are legally required to stop, whether it's for a traffic stop or after a crash. "Fleeing from law enforcement or leaving the scene of a crash can have serious consequences," the department said.

entry.title: As Buc-ee's nears construction, development interest builds in northern St. Lucie County - cbs12.com
entry.summary: As Buc-ee's nears construction, development interest builds in northern St. Lucie County    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Buc-ee’s may be best known for its massive travel centers, barbecue sandwiches and loyal fan base, but on the Treasure Coast, county leaders say the proposed development could signal something even bigger: a wave of growth along the Indrio Road corridor in northern St. After years of planning and review, the proposed Buc-ee’s at Interstate 95 and Indrio Road has completed the county’s planning process, bringing the long-discussed project one step closer to reality. The proposed 76,000-square-foot travel center would feature approximately 120 fuel pumps and could become the largest Buc-ee’s location in Florida. Buc-ee’s Nearing Construction Phase According to St. Lucie County Planning and Development Services Director Benjamin Balcer, the project has cleared its local planning hurdles. "They are completely 100% finished with the planning process," Balcer said. "Our board will not see this again." Balcer said the company is now awaiting final approvals from the Florida Department of Transportation and the Florida Department of Environmental Protection before construction can begin. "As far as the county is concerned, their building permit and their site development permit is pretty much at the tail end and ready to go," Balcer said. "It's really just pulling the trigger on Buc-ee's end to start the process." Buc-ee's has previously targeted a 2028 opening date. Development Interest Growing Along Indrio Road While the travel center itself would bring jobs and tax revenue, county officials say its presence also shines a spotlight on a corridor already attracting significant development interest. For now, much of the area remains undeveloped, with cattle grazing across wide stretches of rural land. But Balcer said developers are increasingly looking at opportunities along Indrio Road. "It's kind of an untapped resource," he said. "At the moment, we're seeing a lot of development interest, whether that's pre-application meetings, developers coming in and talking about concept plans, or actual formal applications." Balcer stopped short of calling Buc-ee's the direct catalyst for that interest, but acknowledged that a major national company can influence future investment decisions. "I don't know if Buc-ee's is a catalyst that actually drives development," he said. "But whenever you have a large national commercial entity like Buc-ee's, it does move the needle whenever people see that type of investment." Why the Corridor Is Attracting Attention The area has benefited from recent road and utility improvements, making it increasingly attractive for future residential and commercial projects. County officials say they are already seeing proposals emerge throughout the area. "But all through that Indrio Road corridor, we do see more retail, mixed-use residential projects that are starting to come in and gain traction," Balcer said. Several large developments are either proposed or moving through the review process near the future Buc-ee's site. The proposed Club at Indrio Creek , located south of Indrio Road, could bring hundreds of new homes to the area. Another proposal, Indrio Town Center , would transform approximately 85 acres near Indrio Road and Emerson Avenue into a mixed-use development featuring retail, office space and residential uses. Perhaps the most controversial proposal was Indrio Groves , a development planned near Spanish Lakes Fairways that could add more than 3,000 homes to the area. The size of that proposal has raised concerns among nearby residents who worry about traffic and infrastructure demands. The discussion was tabled over the summer. Residents Voice Infrastructure Concerns But as development proposals continue to stack up, some residents worry infrastructure isn't keeping pace. "That's what people are concerned about," said Jeff Bourassa, president of the Spanish Lakes Fairways Homeowners Association. If they put another 3,000 homes, we're in trouble." Bourassa said residents are worried local roads are not equipped to handle the level of growth being proposed. They're cowpaths," Bourassa said. "There's nothing that was put in for infrastructure." County officials say they understand those concerns. "People are concerned," Balcer said. "Traffic impacts, changing their lifestyle. This is a historical agricultural kind of community." Looking Ahead Whether Buc-ee's ultimately becomes a transformational project remains to be seen. County leaders say the larger story is what comes next for the surrounding area. If Buc-ee's opens and several proposed developments move forward, the character of the Indrio Road corridor could change dramatically over the next decade. "If Buc-ee's does come online, and the projects that are in the pipeline do develop," Balcer said, "you'll see a big difference in the Indrio Road corridor."

entry.summary: Port St. Lucie man accused of repeatedly sexually assaulting 16-year-old relative    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Lucie man was arrested after police said a 16-year-old relative accused him of sexually assaulting her multiple times inside their shared home. Jean Emile Revange faces three felony counts of sexual battery on a person between the ages of 12 and 17 without physical force likely to cause serious injury, according to a Port St. Lucie Police Department arrest affidavit. The investigation began Sept. 26 after police were notified about allegations involving a teen receiving treatment at Lawnwood Regional Medical Center . According to the affidavit, the teen’s family had taken her to a hospital after she complained of severe abdominal and pelvic pain. During treatment, she disclosed that Revange, who is her father’s cousin, had sexually assaulted her, investigators said. Police said Revange, his wife, the teen and several other relatives lived together in the same Port St. During an interview at the hospital and a subsequent forensic interview at the Children’s Advocacy Center , the teen repeatedly identified Revange as the person who assaulted her, according to the affidavit. Investigators said the teen had cognitive and developmental limitations that affected how she communicated. Police ended their initial detailed questioning so a specially trained forensic interviewer could speak with her. The teen described multiple alleged assaults in different parts of the home. She could not provide exact dates but believed at least one occurred Sept. 23, according to the affidavit. See also: Florida mother leaves 4 children home alone while on Carnival cruise to Bahamas: Police Police later arranged a controlled telephone call between the teen’s father and Revange. According to the detective, Revange initially denied the allegations but later made statements indicating that what the teen said had happened was true. entry.summary: Rabies alert issued in Martin County after raccoon tests positive in Stuart    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: A rabid raccoon found in Stuart prompted the Florida Department of Health in Martin County to issue a 60-day alert Wednesday. The raccoon was captured Sunday off South Kanner Highway and later tested positive for rabies , according to the department. The alert covered an area bounded by Southeast Tressler Drive to the south, Southeast Federal Highway to the east and South Kanner Highway to the west. Health officials said rabies was present among wild animals in the area and urged residents and visitors to avoid contact with raccoons, bats, foxes, skunks, otters, bobcats, coyotes and other wildlife. Rabies is a deadly viral disease most commonly transmitted through the bite or scratch of an infected animal. An animal with rabies may appear healthy and can behave unusually friendly or aggressively. People who are bitten or scratched by a wild or domestic animal should wash the wound with soap and water, seek medical attention and report the incident to the Department of Health in Martin County at 772-221-4030 . Treatment administered after an exposure can prevent the disease. Officials recommended that residents take several precautions: Keep pets and livestock current on rabies vaccinations. Keep pets leashed and under direct supervision. Avoid handling or feeding wild and stray animals. Do not leave pet food or unsecured garbage outdoors. Prevent bats and other wildlife from entering homes, schools and other occupied buildings. Contact a licensed wildlife rehabilitator rather than bringing a wild animal into a home. See also: Florida mother leaves 4 children home alone while on Carnival cruise to Bahamas: Police Anyone whose pet or livestock is bitten should immediately contact a veterinarian and Martin County Animal Control at 772-463-3211 . Residents can also call animal control to report stray animals in their neighborhoods. More information is available at FloridaHealth.gov/Rabies .

entry.article_text: Lucie County Fire District's attorney resigned minutes after a heated special fire board meeting Wednesday, as fallout from an alleged hazing investigation continues to threaten district leadership.Attorney Kim Sabol submitted her resignation letter effective in 90 days. She is the subject of several complaints stemming from allegations that she and Fire Chief Jeff Lee improperly handled internal investigations.WATCH BELOW: St. Lucie County fire district attorney resigns amid hazing falloutNearly a dozen people spoke at the special meeting, which was called to address what board members described as a major gap in district policy: who investigates complaints against the district's own leaders."Since this district's inception, we have not had a policy on how they handle complaints against themselves," St. Lucie County Commissioner and Fire District Board Member Jamie Fowler said. "They — being those positions— have essentially been able to investigate themselves." Those contract positions include the Fire Chief, District Attorney, Clerk Treasurer and Medical Director.The issue stems from an alleged hazing incident we reported on earlier this year. A third-party investigator concluded that videos showing firefighters using a modified bug zapper to shock probationary firefighters depicted hazing. Three veteran firefighters — Doug Boudrias, Jordan Hutchinson and Christopher Baldwin — were fired as a result."It was just us in our downtime, joking around, having fun," Hutchinson said."We're all still friends," Boudrias said. "Us and the victims, there was no ill intent." Months before the incident came to light, Baldwin and Hutchinson filed a complaint against Fire Chief Jeff Lee and Sabol in September 2025. District officials ultimately denied it. Baldwin and Hutchinson then filed additional complaints, including an amended complaint to investigators alleging the hazing investigation — and their subsequent termination — were part of a broader pattern of retaliation."That's not a good process," Fowler said. The board is now asking two outside law firms to help draft a new complaint policy. Meanwhile, firefighters are casting ballots in a no-confidence vote regarding Lee."It basically says whether or not they trust and believe in him to lead this district," Fowler said. "So that is a huge thing if you have the majority of the men and women underneath you saying they can no longer serve under you, that's a pretty impactful message." Lee acknowledged the district lacks a clear complaint process. He told Investigative Reporter Kate Hussey: "I'm glad this board is finally taking this as a serious issue," adding he "welcomes any investigation from any agency."Per Sabol's resignation, Lee said it's a "sad day." "She's been a tremendous attorney for the district," Lee said of Sabol. As for the vote of no confidence, Lee said he didn't have much to say until it's over with "We'll see what the men and women decide," Lee told Hussey. "I came up on the labor side; I've always fought for our men and women on the line." Tension inside district headquarters was evident throughout Wednesday's meeting."This system is so broken," one attendee said."Everybody is fed up. They want action," said retired fire captain Mike Jenkins.As the union's legal fight to reinstate the three firefighters continues, calls are growing for the fire board to bypass arbitration and bring them back to work. When asked whether the board has that authority, Fowler said, "I think we might actually," adding, "The chief wants them back. The union is saying they want to come back. I'm going to ask the board in a week from now — what do we want to do? What's the process?" Firefighters are still casting ballots in the no-confidence vote. entry.title: Dolphins rule out rookie WR Caleb Douglas for second straight week with ankle injury
entry.summary: The Miami Dolphins will be without rookie receiver Caleb Douglas for a second straight game as he continues nursing an ankle injury suffered in Week 2. Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Friday that Douglas and defensive end Robert Beal Jr. (hamstring) will miss Sunday's game at Minnesota, but Miami will have veteran center Aaron Brewer, who appeared on Thursday's injury report with a hand issue. 'He's in every meeting, and hes got to stay locked in, and hes got to watch practice, watch the practice tape, and stay on top of it,' Hafley said of Douglas missing what could be valuable reps early in the season, 'because what we dont want to have happen is when he gets back and hopefully thats soon that he takes a step back mentally. Hes doing a good job, hes a mature guy. Douglas, who has seven receptions for 117 yards in two games, has not practiced the past two weeks after suffering the injury in the second half of a loss at San Francisco. He was one of the standouts in the preseason and was expected to emerge as one of the top targets for quarterback Malik Willis. With Douglas sidelined, fellow rookie Chris Bell, who has still been ramping up from a knee injury suffered last year, had four receptions for 64 yards in last week's loss to Kansas City . Receiver Malik Washington had five catches for 56 yards, and tight end Greg Dulcich added five catches for 55 yards. Hafley said he wants to see improvement in the timing and rhythm with Willis' connection with his young receiving corps. For this team, right now where were at with the youth, with guys playing together, its Can I trust the guy next to me to do his job precisely and be where hes supposed to be every single play over and over again,'' Hafley said. 'And weve seen glimpses of that. And then weve seen where were just a little bit off here and a little bit off here.' Running back Jaylen Wright is expected to return after missing last week with a stinger and foot injury. The Dolphins will lean on the third-year running back a lot more going forward after losing Pro Bowler De'Von Achane to a season-ending ACL tear . Wright and third-stringer Ollie Gordon will see increased roles, and the Dolphins will elevate one of their practice squad running backs, either Carlos Washington Jr. or Jarquez Hunter, for Sunday's game. Also Friday, Hafley said second-year defensive tackle Kenneth Grant could return to practice next week after beginning the season on injured reserve because of a lower-body injury.

"And so a ladder truck is vital to protecting those, those type of occupancies."Palm Beach County Fire Rescue continues to serve nearby unincorporated areas, including county pockets near the Jupiter Inlet, DuBois Park and Jonathan's Landing, Donatto said.Jupiter's first ladder truck features an American flag design and imagery of the Jupiter Lighthouse. Before adopting the tribute, Town of Jupiter officials contacted FDNY Ladder 10 to seek their blessing.Rodman Leas, a firefighter with Jupiter Fire Rescue, explained the significance behind the tribute."Today marks a brand new chapter in Jupiter fire history as we roll out 10 Truck, our community is, like you said, our community's very first ladder truck ever," Leas said. "It carries the number 10 badge ... as we honor FDNY Truck 10, whose firehouse stands directly across from the Sept. 11th World Trade Center site." Leas said six members of FDNY Ladder 10 made the ultimate sacrifice on Sept. 11."I took an inspiration from their American flag design as well ... as a constant reminder of the bravery, courage, brotherhood that defined the fire service," Leas said.Battalion Chief Jason Bohan said Jupiter Fire Rescue worked with Palm Beach Gardens as crews prepared for the new department's launch."We've had an incredible partnership with Palm Beach Gardens," Bohan said. "We've been using their training facility, and because of that partnership over the last couple of months, they and us have been training, getting ready for today."That preparation includes learning to put on approximately 60 pounds of protective equipment quickly when an emergency call comes in.Bohan said the most exciting part of launch day was bringing the new department together around its public service mission."Getting us all together, knowing what we're called to do, which is to protect and save people," Bohan said. "So now that it finally came today, we're all really excited."For Lt. Christian Lainhart, joining Jupiter Fire Rescue also represents a personal homecoming. Lainhart previously worked for Martin County Fire Rescue and described himself as a sixth-generation Jupiter pioneer."I'm super excited, very blessed to be here," Lainhart said.Lainhart said his family's roots in the Jupiter area extend to the 1890s. He grew up and attended school in Jupiter and is now raising his family there."It's just truly remarkable," Lainhart said. "Growing up here, I'm a sixth-generation pioneer, so that really means something here. Grew up here, went to school here, currently raising my family, and now I'm here serving the community that I know and love."While Jupiter's new stations, apparatus and equipment are central to the launch, Donatto said the department's personnel are what make the milestone meaningful."The most exciting thing is the people in it," Donatto said. "We've just been so incredibly blessed to hire some of the best people in the world. entry.title: FDLE testimony focuses on RFP process in ex-Fort Pierce manager Nick Mimms' trial - cbs12.com
entry.summary: FDLE testimony focuses on RFP process in ex-Fort Pierce manager Nick Mimms' trial    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Former Fort Pierce City Manager Nick Mimms is on trial over allegations that he improperly influenced a city bidding process involving two vacant lots in Fort Pierce's Lincoln Park area. Mimms faces charges of bid tampering and official misconduct. He has pleaded not guilty. Prosecutors allege he steered the process toward Lincoln Park Young Professionals, a nonprofit whose board included Mimms' niece and another city employee. On Thursday, much of the testimony focused on who controlled the RFP process and how closely Mimms remained involved after it was turned over to the city's purchasing department. FDLE Agent Derek Brisky testified about emails and other records collected during the investigation. One focus was the nearby Lincoln Theater and its need for parking. Brisky testified Mimms had told the Fort Pierce Redevelopment Agency that the RFP would include language addressing the theater's parking needs. But that language was not included in the request Mimms sent to the purchasing department. Brisky also testified investigators found no evidence Mimms filed a 2019 memorandum concerning the parking plans in the relevant city records. The defense questioned the significance of that omission and emphasized that the purchasing department was responsible for putting together and publishing the RFP after receiving the project's specifications. See also: NTSB report clarifies Amazon plane crash timeline that killed 5 on Sept. 6 Defense attorneys also challenged the state's characterization of the process as a sole-source arrangement. Brisky acknowledged the RFP was not technically a sole-source contract. The state, meanwhile, pointed to emails showing Mimms continued to communicate with city employees about the RFP, including its evaluation criteria and the evaluation committee. Other emails showed city employees knew there had been one submission after the RFP was posted. An LPYP email address was copied on one of those communications. The defense also questioned the investigation's treatment of other city employees involved in the process, including a purchasing official who was not charged. Later, former Fort Pierce employee Kalita Scott testified about LPYP and its efforts to develop the Lincoln Park properties. She described the organization as a group of young professionals focused on community development and said the need for parking near the Lincoln Theater was known in the community. Prosecutors allege Mimms manipulated the city's process to ensure LPYP received the lease. The defense has argued Mimms did not improperly favor the organization and that the evidence does not establish a criminal conspiracy. The trial is continuing in St.

Skid loaders were working along the narrow roadway beside the Indian River Lagoon, adding dirt and sand to reinforce an area where erosion has left the road’s edge vulnerable. Crews brought 32 loads of dirt to the site Sept. But only days later, the embankment again needed repairs. Resident Gene Barnes said the recurring work is not a long-term solution. We’re losing ground year by year, Barnes said. Until the Corps of Engineers or something like that comes and puts a headwall in to stabilize it, it’s not going to be an easy fix. The road has faced erosion problems before. Heavy rain damaged sections in 2014, and Hurricane Nicole caused additional washouts in 2022. Barnes said continued rain and tidal action could undermine the roadway itself. See also: Case reopened: Port St. Lucie TikTok creator jailed on computer-access charge If we keep getting rains like this, it’s going to undermine the road, and then the road is going to collapse and the school bus is going to fall in the hole, he said. While repairs on South Indian River Drive may be less costly, residents said the erosion is likely to remain a concern as more rain and tidal action are forecast.

entry.title: As Buc-ee's nears construction, development interest builds in northern St. Lucie County - WPEC
entry.summary: As Buc-ee's nears construction, development interest builds in northern St. Lucie County    WPEC
entry.article_text: Buc-ee’s may be best known for its massive travel centers, barbecue sandwiches and loyal fan base, but on the Treasure Coast, county leaders say the proposed development could signal something even bigger: a wave of growth along the Indrio Road corridor in northern St. After years of planning and review, the proposed Buc-ee’s at Interstate 95 and Indrio Road has completed the county’s planning process, bringing the long-discussed project one step closer to reality. The proposed 76,000-square-foot travel center would feature approximately 120 fuel pumps and could become the largest Buc-ee’s location in Florida. Buc-ee’s Nearing Construction Phase According to St. Lucie County Planning and Development Services Director Benjamin Balcer, the project has cleared its local planning hurdles. "They are completely 100% finished with the planning process," Balcer said. "Our board will not see this again." Balcer said the company is now awaiting final approvals from the Florida Department of Transportation and the Florida Department of Environmental Protection before construction can begin. "As far as the county is concerned, their building permit and their site development permit is pretty much at the tail end and ready to go," Balcer said. "It's really just pulling the trigger on Buc-ee's end to start the process." Buc-ee's has previously targeted a 2028 opening date. Development Interest Growing Along Indrio Road While the travel center itself would bring jobs and tax revenue, county officials say its presence also shines a spotlight on a corridor already attracting significant development interest. For now, much of the area remains undeveloped, with cattle grazing across wide stretches of rural land. But Balcer said developers are increasingly looking at opportunities along Indrio Road. "It's kind of an untapped resource," he said. "At the moment, we're seeing a lot of development interest, whether that's pre-application meetings, developers coming in and talking about concept plans, or actual formal applications." Balcer stopped short of calling Buc-ee's the direct catalyst for that interest, but acknowledged that a major national company can influence future investment decisions. "I don't know if Buc-ee's is a catalyst that actually drives development," he said. "But whenever you have a large national commercial entity like Buc-ee's, it does move the needle whenever people see that type of investment." Why the Corridor Is Attracting Attention The area has benefited from recent road and utility improvements, making it increasingly attractive for future residential and commercial projects. County officials say they are already seeing proposals emerge throughout the area. "But all through that Indrio Road corridor, we do see more retail, mixed-use residential projects that are starting to come in and gain traction," Balcer said. Several large developments are either proposed or moving through the review process near the future Buc-ee's site. The proposed Club at Indrio Creek , located south of Indrio Road, could bring hundreds of new homes to the area. Another proposal, Indrio Town Center , would transform approximately 85 acres near Indrio Road and Emerson Avenue into a mixed-use development featuring retail, office space and residential uses. Perhaps the most controversial proposal was Indrio Groves , a development planned near Spanish Lakes Fairways that could add more than 3,000 homes to the area. The size of that proposal has raised concerns among nearby residents who worry about traffic and infrastructure demands. The discussion was tabled over the summer. Residents Voice Infrastructure Concerns But as development proposals continue to stack up, some residents worry infrastructure isn't keeping pace. "That's what people are concerned about," said Jeff Bourassa, president of the Spanish Lakes Fairways Homeowners Association. If they put another 3,000 homes, we're in trouble." Bourassa said residents are worried local roads are not equipped to handle the level of growth being proposed. They're cowpaths," Bourassa said. "There's nothing that was put in for infrastructure." County officials say they understand those concerns. "People are concerned," Balcer said. "Traffic impacts, changing their lifestyle. This is a historical agricultural kind of community." Looking Ahead Whether Buc-ee's ultimately becomes a transformational project remains to be seen. County leaders say the larger story is what comes next for the surrounding area. If Buc-ee's opens and several proposed developments move forward, the character of the Indrio Road corridor could change dramatically over the next decade. "If Buc-ee's does come online, and the projects that are in the pipeline do develop," Balcer said, "you'll see a big difference in the Indrio Road corridor."

entry.title: 'Not knowing where he is': Family searches for missing Port St. Lucie father - WPEC
entry.summary: 'Not knowing where he is': Family searches for missing Port St. Lucie father    WPEC
entry.article_text: Eight months after a Port St. Lucie father vanished, his family says they are still searching for answers and living with the painful uncertainty of not knowing where he is. "I'm stuck in this cycle of not knowing where he is," said Aubrey Finley, whose brother, Robert La Polla , disappeared Jan. 8 after being released from a hospital in Fort Pierce. The 47-year-old father has not been seen or heard from since, according to his family. Detectives have no confirmed sightings, and the case remains unsolved. Finley said La Polla struggled with depression following the deaths of their parents, but the siblings remained close and talked often. "Everything kind of fell apart," she said. "But we still managed to communicate a lot. We were still there for each other all the time." Also read: Search underway for missing autistic man last seen at Jensen Beach home Thursday morning Because of that bond, Finley said her brother's disappearance is completely out of character. In the months since he vanished, family members and friends have organized search efforts across Fort Pierce, checking wooded areas and busy corridors near HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. "We've gone through woods, under bridges, talking to people everywhere in Fort Pierce, trying to find anything that brings us to him," Finley said. The search has also taken an emotional toll on La Polla's young daughter, who continues to wait for her father to come home. She misses him," Finley said. "He's got a family that love him." The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office (SLCSO) said La Polla has been entered into a national missing persons database. Investigators have also collected DNA from family members in case it is needed for identification and continue to follow up on leads. Anyone with information about La Polla's whereabouts is asked to contact Detective Cpl. Drawdy at 772-462-3230 or call 911.

entry.title: Case reopened: Port St. Lucie TikTok creator jailed on computer-access charge - cw34.com
entry.summary: Case reopened: Port St. Lucie TikTok creator jailed on computer-access charge    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Lucie man whose TikTok and Twich bios identify him as a cybersecurity engineer was jailed Wednesday after police reopened an investigation that had been closed in May. Mark Stephen Asea, 36, was booked into the St. Lucie County Jail on Sept. on one pending count of offense against computer users, according to jail records. His bond was set at $35,000. An earlier stalking charge appears to have been dropped. The charge stems from an earlier investigation in which detectives accused Asea of gaining access to women’s electronic devices and using TikTok posts to discuss information they said was private. In a warrant affidavit, a detective described reviewing videos from an account linked to Asea. The profile’s bio identifies its user as a narcissistic abuse survivor, former satanist, empath, cybersecurity engineer and woodsman. Police said one video included references to a woman’s password, device information, banking activity, license plate number and possible location tracking. The woman told investigators the password had been shared only in a closed TikTok group chat and that she had not given Asea permission to share it. Another woman told police Asea previously had remote access to her computer to help with an application. She became concerned, investigators said, after an image from a private Telegram message appeared in one of his TikTok posts. See also: Florida Education Department eyes dress code to ban head coverings, Crocs, short skirts The earlier affidavit alleged Asea posted more than 100 TikTok videos mentioning one of the women, including as many as six in a day. Detectives also cited videos that appeared to show computer equipment and coding as they investigated whether he had accessed devices without authorization. Asea’s booking photo shows him with long dark hair and prominent geometric tattoos across his face.
