entry.title: Altercation at tow yard leads to shooting, Martin County Sheriff's Office says - WPBF
entry.summary: Altercation at tow yard leads to shooting, Martin County Sheriff's Office says    WPBF
entry.article_text: The Martin County Sheriff’s Office is actively investigating after a shooting Friday afternoon at Gary's Towing and Recovery near Stuart. At 1 p.m., deputies responded to Southeast Cove Road at 4405 SE Cove Road. A woman from Miami arrived at the tow yard to claim a vehicle that had been towed there earlier in the day. Then, people in another vehicle arrived at the facility, and the two parties became involved in an altercation, according to the sheriff's office. https://www.facebook.com/MartinCountySheriffsOffice/posts/pfbid0enPBfuxCWxva9Ce6vmU7hGP3nKdhfidsLzp1e7zxkZ58uSYxB3KhHPTdVi9kagZnl The Miami woman then retrieved a firearm and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before getting into a vehicle and fleeing the area, the agency said. Because the tow yard is about a half-mile from Murray Middle School, the sheriff’s office activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout as deputies responded to the scene. Road Patrol deputies, aviation, detectives and other available units began searching for the suspect vehicle. Deputies located the vehicle traveling on Cove Road near U.S. 1 and attempted a traffic stop. The driver fled, and deputies subsequently performed a PIT maneuver, bringing the vehicle to a stop, MCSO said. Additional units moved in and successfully immobilized the vehicle before the driver could flee again. The individuals targeted by the gunfire had left the area before deputies arrived. At this time, it is unclear whether any of them were struck by gunfire, the agency said. The woman was taken into custody and taken to the Sheriff’s Office, where detectives are currently questioning her. entry.summary: Port St. Lucie man sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Stuart vape shop shooting    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie man convicted in connection with a shooting inside a Stuart vape shop has been sentenced to decades in prison, police said Friday. Joshua Gibbs was sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Florida state prison, followed by 10 years of probation, according to the Stuart Police Department. The sentence stems from the Jan. 25, 2025, shooting at Miller’s Vapory, 1596 SE Federal Highway. Police said Gibbs, then 19, entered the business wearing a ski mask and carrying a handgun before firing at a store clerk. The clerk fired back, and no one was injured. Detectives identified Gibbs as the suspect following an extensive investigation, police said. Authorities arrested him in Douglasville, Georgia, with help from the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force. See also: Ag Reserve meeting draws overflow crowd, tense atmosphere in Delray Beach Police previously said Gibbs had confronted the clerk in December 2024 after he was denied service because he was underage. Investigators said he threatened the clerk and stole more than $300 in vape products. Gibbs was initially accused of attempted robbery with a firearm, aggravated assault with a firearm and robbery without a firearm in connection with the earlier theft.

entry.title: Miami woman in custody after shooting at tow yard near Murray Middle School in Martin County
entry.summary: A shooting at a tow yard Friday afternoon near a middle school in Martin County triggered a lockout and led to a chase and a Miami woman in custody. The woman opened fire at a tow yard on Southeast Cove Road shortly after 1 p.m., the Martin County Sheriff's Office said. According to deputies, the woman arrived at the towing facility to claim a car that had been towed there earlier in the day. Shortly after, individuals in another car arrived at the facility, and the two parties became involved in an altercation, deputies said. The woman got a gun and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before getting into a car and leaving the area. Since the tow yard is located near Murray Middle School, the sheriff's office said it immediately activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout as deputies responded to the scene. Road patrol deputies, aviation, detectives and other available units quickly began searching for the woman's car, deputies said, and located the car traveling on Cove Road near U.S. 1 Deputies said they attempted a traffic stop but the driver fled, forcing deputies to perform a PIT maneuver, bringing the car to a stop. The individuals who were shot at left the area before deputies arrived, the sheriff's office said. It is unclear whether any of them were struck by gunfire. The woman was taken into custody and transported to the sheriff's office, where detectives are currently questioning her. Deputies said additional information will be provided as it becomes available.

entry.title: Rabies alert issued in Indian River County after rabid bat found near apartment complex
entry.summary: The Florida Department of Health in Indian River County has issued a 60-day rabies alert after a bat captured near the Sonrise Apartments tested positive for the virus. Health officials said the bat was captured in the Sonrise Apartments area off Sonrise Place in Fellsmere on Sept. 24. Anyone who may have had contact with or touched the bat is urged to contact the Department of Health in Indian River County at 772-794-7472. WATCH BELOW: Rabid bat prompts alert in Indian River County Rabid bat prompts alert in Indian River County The alert comes as health officials monitor rabies activity among wild animals in the area and warn residents that the disease is present in the local wildlife population. Rabies is a viral disease that affects the nervous system of mammals, including humans. Health officials say people who are exposed to rabies can protect themselves by seeking prompt medical treatment after exposure. The Department of Health is reminding residents and visitors to avoid contact with wild animals such as raccoons, bats, foxes, skunks, otters, bobcats and coyotes, which are more likely to carry the disease. Officials also recommend taking several precautions to reduce the risk of exposure, including: Keeping pets vaccinated against rabies Supervising pets and keeping them on a leash Securing livestock on private property Avoiding contact with wild or stray animals, including cats Not feeding or handling wildlife Preventing bats and other wildlife from entering homes, schools and other occupied buildings Anyone bitten or scratched by a wild or domestic animal should seek medical attention and report the incident to the Department of Health in Indian River County at 772-794-7472. If a pet or livestock animal is bitten by another animal, owners should contact a veterinarian immediately and notify Indian River County Animal Control at 772-226-4799. Visit the Florida Department of Health website for more information on rabies.

Jean Emile Revange faces three felony counts of sexual battery on a person between the ages of 12 and 17 without physical force likely to cause serious injury, according to a Port St. Lucie Police Department arrest affidavit. The investigation began Sept. 26 after police were notified about allegations involving a teen receiving treatment at Lawnwood Regional Medical Center . According to the affidavit, the teen’s family had taken her to a hospital after she complained of severe abdominal and pelvic pain. During treatment, she disclosed that Revange, who is her father’s cousin, had sexually assaulted her, investigators said. Investigators said the teen had cognitive and developmental limitations that affected how she communicated. Police ended their initial detailed questioning so a specially trained forensic interviewer could speak with her. The teen described multiple alleged assaults in different parts of the home. She could not provide exact dates but believed at least one occurred Sept. 23, according to the affidavit. After Revange was taken into custody, however, he denied the allegations during an interview conducted in Creole, the affidavit said. entry.summary: Woman in custody after Martin County tow yard shooting leads to pursuit, PIT maneuver    WPEC
entry.article_text: A woman is in custody after deputies say an altercation at a Martin County towing facility escalated into gunfire, triggering a law enforcement response, a school lockout and a pursuit Friday afternoon. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office , the shooting happened shortly after 1 p.m. at a towing facility on Southeast Cove Road. Investigators said a woman from Miami arrived at the tow yard to retrieve a vehicle that had been towed there earlier in the day. Shortly afterward, people in another vehicle arrived at the facility and became involved in an altercation with the woman, according to MCSO. The sheriff's office said the woman retrieved a firearm and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before getting into a vehicle and fleeing the area. Because the tow yard is about a half-mile from Murray Middle School , the sheriff's office activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout while deputies responded. See also: Woman arrested at Mar-a-Lago after claiming Sen. Tom Cotton invited her Road patrol deputies, aviation units, detectives and other available units began searching for the suspect vehicle. Deputies located the vehicle traveling on Cove Road near U.S. 1 and attempted a traffic stop, according to MCSO. The sheriff's office said the driver fled, prompting deputies to perform a PIT maneuver to stop the vehicle. Additional units moved in and immobilized the vehicle before the driver could flee again, according to MCSO. The woman was taken into custody and transported to the Martin County Sheriff's Office, where detectives were questioning her. The people who were allegedly targeted by the gunfire left the towing facility before deputies arrived. As of the sheriff's office's latest update, investigators did not know whether anyone had been struck by gunfire. Murray Middle School sent out the following message to families: "Good afternoon, Lions! Please note that we have heavy police presence in the area for an incident unrelated to Murray. We are following Martin County Sheriffs Office guidance and are on a lock out. We will remain in close contact with them and provide additional information as it becomes available. Thank you, Principal Roth" The sheriff's office has not released the woman's identity or announced any charges. The investigation remains active.

entry.title: As Buc-ee's nears construction, development interest builds in northern St. Lucie County - cw34.com
entry.summary: As Buc-ee's nears construction, development interest builds in northern St. Lucie County    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Buc-ee’s may be best known for its massive travel centers, barbecue sandwiches and loyal fan base, but on the Treasure Coast, county leaders say the proposed development could signal something even bigger: a wave of growth along the Indrio Road corridor in northern St. After years of planning and review, the proposed Buc-ee’s at Interstate 95 and Indrio Road has completed the county’s planning process, bringing the long-discussed project one step closer to reality. The proposed 76,000-square-foot travel center would feature approximately 120 fuel pumps and could become the largest Buc-ee’s location in Florida. Buc-ee’s Nearing Construction Phase According to St. Lucie County Planning and Development Services Director Benjamin Balcer, the project has cleared its local planning hurdles. "They are completely 100% finished with the planning process," Balcer said. "Our board will not see this again." Balcer said the company is now awaiting final approvals from the Florida Department of Transportation and the Florida Department of Environmental Protection before construction can begin. "As far as the county is concerned, their building permit and their site development permit is pretty much at the tail end and ready to go," Balcer said. "It's really just pulling the trigger on Buc-ee's end to start the process." Buc-ee's has previously targeted a 2028 opening date. Development Interest Growing Along Indrio Road While the travel center itself would bring jobs and tax revenue, county officials say its presence also shines a spotlight on a corridor already attracting significant development interest. For now, much of the area remains undeveloped, with cattle grazing across wide stretches of rural land. But Balcer said developers are increasingly looking at opportunities along Indrio Road. "It's kind of an untapped resource," he said. "At the moment, we're seeing a lot of development interest, whether that's pre-application meetings, developers coming in and talking about concept plans, or actual formal applications." Balcer stopped short of calling Buc-ee's the direct catalyst for that interest, but acknowledged that a major national company can influence future investment decisions. "I don't know if Buc-ee's is a catalyst that actually drives development," he said. "But whenever you have a large national commercial entity like Buc-ee's, it does move the needle whenever people see that type of investment." Why the Corridor Is Attracting Attention The area has benefited from recent road and utility improvements, making it increasingly attractive for future residential and commercial projects. County officials say they are already seeing proposals emerge throughout the area. "But all through that Indrio Road corridor, we do see more retail, mixed-use residential projects that are starting to come in and gain traction," Balcer said. Several large developments are either proposed or moving through the review process near the future Buc-ee's site. The proposed Club at Indrio Creek , located south of Indrio Road, could bring hundreds of new homes to the area. Another proposal, Indrio Town Center , would transform approximately 85 acres near Indrio Road and Emerson Avenue into a mixed-use development featuring retail, office space and residential uses. Perhaps the most controversial proposal was Indrio Groves , a development planned near Spanish Lakes Fairways that could add more than 3,000 homes to the area. The size of that proposal has raised concerns among nearby residents who worry about traffic and infrastructure demands. The discussion was tabled over the summer. Residents Voice Infrastructure Concerns But as development proposals continue to stack up, some residents worry infrastructure isn't keeping pace. "That's what people are concerned about," said Jeff Bourassa, president of the Spanish Lakes Fairways Homeowners Association. If they put another 3,000 homes, we're in trouble." Bourassa said residents are worried local roads are not equipped to handle the level of growth being proposed. They're cowpaths," Bourassa said. "There's nothing that was put in for infrastructure." County officials say they understand those concerns. "People are concerned," Balcer said. "Traffic impacts, changing their lifestyle. This is a historical agricultural kind of community." Looking Ahead Whether Buc-ee's ultimately becomes a transformational project remains to be seen. County leaders say the larger story is what comes next for the surrounding area. If Buc-ee's opens and several proposed developments move forward, the character of the Indrio Road corridor could change dramatically over the next decade. "If Buc-ee's does come online, and the projects that are in the pipeline do develop," Balcer said, "you'll see a big difference in the Indrio Road corridor."

entry.article_text: Lucie man convicted in connection with a shooting inside a Stuart vape shop has been sentenced to decades in prison, police said Friday. Joshua Gibbs was sentenced to 37 1/2 years in Florida state prison, followed by 10 years of probation, according to the Stuart Police Department. The sentence stems from the Jan. 25, 2025, shooting at Miller’s Vapory, 1596 SE Federal Highway. Police said Gibbs, then 19, entered the business wearing a ski mask and carrying a handgun before firing at a store clerk. The clerk fired back, and no one was injured. Detectives identified Gibbs as the suspect following an extensive investigation, police said. Authorities arrested him in Douglasville, Georgia, with help from the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force. See also: Ag Reserve meeting draws overflow crowd, tense atmosphere in Delray Beach Police previously said Gibbs had confronted the clerk in December 2024 after he was denied service because he was underage. Investigators said he threatened the clerk and stole more than $300 in vape products. Gibbs was initially accused of attempted robbery with a firearm, aggravated assault with a firearm and robbery without a firearm in connection with the earlier theft.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie teen named National Youth of the Year by Boys & Girls Clubs of America
entry.summary: A Port St. Lucie teenager has earned the highest honor awarded by the Boys Girls Clubs of America. Enrique Rosario Liz has been named the organizations 2026-27 National Youth of the Year, a recognition that celebrates outstanding leadership, academic achievement and service to others. The honor marks the latest milestone in a remarkable year for Rosario Liz. In April, he was named Florida Youth of the Year. Two months later, he earned the title of Southeast Youth of the Year, advancing to the national level of competition. In July, Rosario Liz received another surprise when the Boys Girls Clubs of America selected him to attend the FIFA World Cup final as a flag bearer. WPTV reporter Tyler Hatfield helped deliver the exciting news during a special presentation. Now, Rosario Liz is being recognized on the national stage as a standout young leader who exemplifies dedication in the classroom, strong personal values and a commitment to serving his community. The National Youth of the Year program honors exceptional teens from Boys Girls Clubs across the country who inspire others through their leadership, character and achievements. Rosario Liz's journey from local club member to national honoree highlights the impact of mentorship, perseverance and community involvement.

entry.summary: Hundreds of residents packed the South County Civic Center on Friday, while many more were turned away, as concerns over development in Palm Beach County's Agricultural Reserve sparked a heated public meeting that at times became contentious. The meeting, hosted by Palm Beach County Commissioner Maria Sachs, focused on approved projects planned for the area, including a DMV office, a nursing home and an Islamic center. Residents raised concerns about traffic, development impacts and whether enough public notice was given before the projects moved forward. Before the meeting even began, tensions were already running high. More than 1,000 people RSVP'd for the event, despite the venue having space for only about 300 attendees. entry.article_text: Hundreds of residents packed the South County Civic Center on Friday, while many more were turned away, as concerns over development in Palm Beach County's Agricultural Reserve sparked a heated public meeting that at times became contentious.The meeting, hosted by Palm Beach County Commissioner Maria Sachs, focused on approved projects planned for the area, including a DMV office, a nursing home and an Islamic center. Residents raised concerns about traffic, development impacts and whether enough public notice was given before the projects moved forward.WATCH BELOW: Overflow crowd, heated debate mark Ag Reserve development meetingBefore the meeting even began, tensions were already running high.More than 1,000 people RSVP'd for the event, despite the venue having space for only about 300 attendees. As crowds gathered outside, many said they were frustrated they could not get inside.Faith Kohn, who traveled from Parkland, said she RSVP'd but never received a response."We all want to be part of this meeting, and they won't let us in," said Kohn. Others outside voiced frustration as they waited outside."We have all these elderly people sweltering in the heat; we're not getting any information, we the people have no respect, they won't let us in to talk or even see the proceedings," said a man standing near the locked front doors as security guarded the entrance.When WPTV reporter Joel Lopez made it inside, there were still chairs available. We learned county officials shut the doors promptly at 9:30 a.m. so the meeting could begin, with Sachs noting she only had until 11 a.m. to get through the discussion.Earlier in the week, WPTV reporter Zitlali Solache reported the meeting had already reached its capacity for RSVPs on Wednesday, and encouraged residents who couldn't secure a seat to watch the meeting online via livestream.Inside the meeting, Sachs found herself fielding concerns from residents who say they want the Agricultural Reserve to remain focused on farming and preservation rather than additional development.When Sachs asked how many people wanted more farming and less housing and school development in the Ag Reserve, the crowd responded overwhelmingly.The discussion quickly turned to concerns over traffic, growth and public notification requirements.Pamela Higer-Polani, an attorney who lives in the Ag Reserve and helped organize residents to attend the meeting.She told WPTV residents have always been vocal about defending the ag reserve, and the fact that many weren't present during the approval process should have been a red flag. "If they did not receive notice, how would they have known that there was supposed to be a commissioner vote or anything of that?" said Pamela Higer-Polani.Higer-Polani said she believes residents living within 1,000 feet of the proposed projects should have been notified, rather than only those within 500 feet."I'm not here how to tell people how to have their religion, how to practice it, that is not my purpose. My purpose is I am extremely concerned that we have had our due process rights violated," said Higer-Polani.At one point during the meeting, Higer-Polani was asked to sit down and was escorted back to her seat by PBSO security after repeatedly attempting to continue her remarks while Sachs worked to restore order.It was one of several moments during the meeting where audience members shouted, stood up and chanted, nearly causing the event to end early as Sachs struggled to regain control.Following the meeting, Sachs told WPTV that residents have every right to express concerns and hold elected officials accountable."People need to be able to voice their opinion on who their neighbors are or aren't, and whether their elected representative listens to them; they can vote them out of office," said Sachs.She also noted she has consistently voted against every development project in the Agricultural Reserve but is only one of seven commissioners.Sachs encouraged residents to contact all county commissioners about their concerns. She explained that the projects residents were protesting were approved through an administrative review process that has existed for years and allows certain government entities and houses of worship to move forward without direct approval from county commissioners."I think for the most part people had their voices heard, but what they said is they want to have a voice in what comes to development in this county. I respect that I hear them," Sachs said.She is now working on a proposal that would require future development applications to come before elected county commissioners for approval."Do you think there's anything that can be done for the developments that have already been approved in the area?" asked Lopez."That's up to the lawyers," said Sachs, adding that she supports looking into it, and that legal action would likely be required to revisit previous approvals.Another major point of contention centered on an Islamic center planned for the Agricultural Reserve.The project was approved in 2022 and was repeatedly discussed during Friday's meeting, calling for stricter background checks and more information about applicants seeking approval for places of worship.Outside the venue, some attendees held signs agaisnt the site and during the meeting, Sachs directed questions regarding the applicant and project funding to attorney Brian Seymour of the Gunster law firm.In response to growing concerns and rhetoric surrounding the project, the Boca Raton Interfaith Clergy Association released the following statement urging respect and tolerance:"As faith leaders in Boca Raton, we believe we live our best lives in a pluralistic, respectful democracy where faith communities live side by side in peace. For decades we have worked together in partnership and mutual respect to build a vibrant, diverse religious community. We write today to urge everyone to seek the peace and welfare of our city and to protect what we have built together.We know some in our community are concerned about plans for expansion, including a new house of worship, in the Agricultural Reserve. Questions about how that area will be developed are before the Palm Beach County Commission and we trust our commissioners to act in the community's best interests.Over the past week we have seen painful and at times hateful remarks about various faith traditions in online conversations about this issue. We condemn unreservedly any expressions of hatred, bigotry, and the vitriol we have seen. We cannot tolerate this level of intolerance.We always encourage residents to bring their concerns to elected officials. We ask that they do so with respect and gratitude for the blessing of a diverse religious community.We stand together in defending every faith community's right to gather and to build houses of worship and community centers. This is a fundamental freedom of our American democracy, and it is essential to living out our commitments to our faiths."-Boca Raton Interfaith Clergy AssociationSachs told WPTV she plans to hold a second public meeting to further discuss the issues raised Friday.A date and location have not been finalized, but Sachs indicated a much larger venue will likely be needed given the turnout.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Our editorial team verifies all reporting on all platforms for fairness and accuracy.

entry.title: 21-year-old Okeechobee woman killed in car crash involving tractor-trailer on State Road 710
entry.summary: The Florida Highway Patrol is investigating a car crash involving a tractor-trailer that killed a 21-year-old Okeechobee woman Thursday afternoon. The deadly accident happened at around 1 p.m. at the T-intersection of State Road 710 and Southeast 86th Boulevard. FHP said the woman was at a stop sign at Southeast 86th Boulevard turning left onto State Road 710, when her car was struck by a man driving a tractor-trailer. The woman failed to yield the right of way, traveling into the tractor-trailers lane of travel, causing the tractor-trailer to collide with the drivers side of the womans car. The woman was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital where she died from her injuries. The man was not injured. FHP said the investigation is ongoing.

entry.title: 'I'm forced to live in this filth': Jensen Beach residents frustrated by recurring septic backups after storms
entry.summary: WPTV is looking into drainage and septic issues on the Treasure Coast. Neighbor Daniel Fletchall reached out to our news team about septic issues in his community on Northwest Sunset Boulevard in Jensen Beach. WATCH BELOW: 'I'm forced to live in this filth': Neighbors demand septic solution Neighbors deal with septic back-ups following heavy rainfall Fletchall said after a heavy rain, he and his neighbors' septic backs up and comes up into their yards 'The sewage water from the septic tank will actually make its way up out of the tank and into my yard,' said Fletchall. 'It smells back here, and I can't let my dog out.' Fletchall said they can't even flush their toilets for days. 'I got to go down to Home Depot or go to the mall to use the bathroom,' said Fletchall. Fletchall added he can't shower or wash his clothes. 'Thankfully, my parents live nearby, so I can go take a shower,' said Fletchall. 'But it's just not happening here. Fletchall isn't the only one affected by this issue. Neighbors like Christie Berger are also having septic issues every time there's heavy rain. 'I go to McDonald's to use the bathroom if I have to,' Berger said. Neighbor Rachelle Kukan said it's becoming unacceptable. 'I wish I could just kind of pick up and move because this is such a problem and it's so serious to me that I would leave if I could,' said Kukan. Fletchall said he had septic companies come out to fix the drainage in his yard. Elevating the septic tank, Fletchall said, would be costly, and even then he's been told it might not solve the problem. Fletchall said he'd like the Martin County staff to extend the sewer lines into his neighborhood. 'I'm forced to live in this filth, and I still pay the taxes every year to have things done around the county, but Im not getting any help here,' said Fletchall. WPTV reached out to Martin County about any solutions. Staff said the neighborhood on Northwest Sunset Boulevard is on the list to get septic-to-sewer conversions, but no date has been set yet. Staff said they're looking at ways to potentially move the neighborhood up on the list of systems to convert.

entry.title: Rising dating costs push Gen Z, millennials toward cheaper date nights
entry.summary: The price of dating is going up, and younger adults are looking for less expensive ways to enjoy a date night, according to new data. Payment app Zelle did some research and found 84% of Gen Z and Millennial daters say rising costs have led them to date less, choose less expensive activities or just stop dating. WATCH BELOW: Gen Z, Millennials seek cheaper date nights, study says Higher Prices Impacts Date Night for Gen Z and Millennials Over half also say they value being thoughtful, honest and transparent with money and prefer planning a budget-friendly date. A few adults in their 20s told me a night with a TV movie and ordering food is usually preferred. Not anything extravagant,' said Nia Pierre. 'I like something that's casual or activity-filled, but it usually starts off like a coffee date or something.' And when it comes to paying for the date, 52% say they don't want to make the situation awkward. 'I would say usually the guy pays, but yeah, it's like a 50-50 thing when deciding if its the guy or girl,' Pierre said.

entry.title: Indiantown flooding remains a problem despite millions spent on drainage - WPEC
entry.summary: Indiantown flooding remains a problem despite millions spent on drainage    WPEC
entry.article_text: Flooding continues to be a problem across Indiantown, leaving some residents questioning why the issue persists despite years of efforts to improve drainage. Large areas of the village saw flooding this week including Booker Park despite spending more than $2 million on drainage improvements in the area in recent years. Residents have seen some improvements over the years but believe more need to be done. I’ve been here almost 60 years and it hasn’t gotten right, Brown said. It is better than it was at some point, but in 60 years you would think it would be far greater than what it is now. The latest round of flooding has affected other parts of Indiantown as well. Oak River saw significant flooding this week, while floodwater also surrounded Indian River Middle School. For residents whose homes take on water, the problem can quickly become a financial burden. Flood insurance can help cover some flood-related damage, but it can also come with a significant cost. For homeowners without a flood policy, recovery can become more difficult. Brian Christensen, president of Coast to Coast Adjuster, said homeowners facing a flood claim without coverage may have to look for other ways to pay for repairs. See also: GALLERY: Ag Reserve meeting draws overflow crowd, tense atmosphere in Delray Beach If you don’t have a flood policy and it is a flood claim and your homeowners policy won’t cut it, I start looking for a loan, Christensen said. Start looking for something a second mortgage, friends, family, churches anything that can assist you. Indiantown Councilman Anthony Dowling said the village is working with Martin County on the flooding problem. The village is also considering a municipal bond that could help address broken pipes and other infrastructure issues. Dowling said the village is repairing pipes that are already damaged and clearing debris from drainage systems. He acknowledged that addressing the flooding problem will not happen overnight and urged residents to take precautions when floodwater is present. I would encourage no kids to play in the water, Dowling said. Village officials say they are continuing to look for ways to address flooding throughout Indiantown. But after years of flooding and millions of dollars spent on drainage improvements residents say they want to know when they will finally see a significant difference.

entry.title: Miami woman in custody after shooting at tow yard near Murray Middle School in Martin County - WFLX
entry.summary: Miami woman in custody after shooting at tow yard near Murray Middle School in Martin County    WFLX
entry.article_text: A shooting at a tow yard Friday afternoon near a middle school in Martin County triggered a lockout and led to a chase and a Miami woman in custody. The woman opened fire at a tow yard on Southeast Cove Road shortly after 1 p.m., the Martin County Sheriff’s Office said. According to deputies, the woman arrived at the towing facility to claim a car that had been towed there earlier in the day. Shortly after, individuals in another car arrived at the facility, and the two parties became involved in an altercation, deputies said. The woman got a gun and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before getting into a car and leaving the area. Since the tow yard is located near Murray Middle School, the sheriff’s office said it immediately activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout as deputies responded to the scene. Road patrol deputies, aviation, detectives and other available units quickly began searching for the woman’s car, deputies said, and located the car traveling on Cove Road near U.S. 1 Deputies said they attempted a traffic stop but the driver fled, forcing deputies to perform a PIT maneuver, bringing the car to a stop. The individuals who were shot at left the area before deputies arrived, the sheriff’s office said. It is unclear whether any of them were struck by gunfire. The woman was taken into custody and transported to the sheriff’s office, where detectives are currently questioning her. Deputies said additional information will be provided as it becomes available.

entry.title: Woman in custody after Martin County tow yard shooting leads to pursuit, PIT maneuver - WPEC
entry.summary: Woman in custody after Martin County tow yard shooting leads to pursuit, PIT maneuver    WPEC
entry.article_text: A second woman has been arrested following a chaotic chain of events that began with a shooting at a Martin County tow yard, triggered a nearby school lockout and ended with multiple crashes and a police pursuit. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office , the incident unfolded shortly after 1 p.m. Friday at Gary's Towing and Recovery on Southeast Cove Road. Investigators said 23-year-old Jade Ely Rondon, of Miami, arrived at the tow yard to retrieve a BMW that had been towed earlier in the day. Deputies said another group arrived shortly afterward, leading to an altercation. According to the sheriff's office, Rondon retrieved a firearm and fired multiple shots at the other individuals before fleeing the scene in a vehicle. Because the business is located about a half-mile from Murray Middle School, deputies activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout while officers searched for the suspect. Deputies later located Rondon's vehicle near U.S. 1 and attempted a traffic stop. Investigators said she refused to stop, prompting deputies to perform a PIT maneuver and take her into custody. Rondon was arrested and charged with two counts of aggravated assault with firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended, and felony criminal mischief. See also: Woman arrested at Mar-a-Lago after claiming Sen. Tom Cotton invited her According to the sheriff's office, Valerie Valdes, 24, had accompanied Rondon to the tow yard to retrieve the BMW. After the shooting, deputies said Valdes fled in the vehicle they originally arrived in and drove recklessly while attempting to leave the area. Investigators said Valdes ultimately crashed at the intersection of Constitutional Boulevard and U.S. She was taken to Cleveland Clinic Martin South Hospital for treatment of her injuries before being arrested. Valdes is charged with operating an unregistered motor vehicle, and four counts of reckless driving with injuries. The people who were allegedly targeted by the gunfire left the towing facility before deputies arrived. CBS12 News spoke with Gary Reed, owner of Gary's Towing and Recovery, who said he's grateful no one was hurt during the incident. Murray Middle School sent out the following message to families: "Good afternoon, Lions! Please note that we have heavy police presence in the area for an incident unrelated to Murray. We are following Martin County Sheriff's Office guidance and are on a lock out. We will remain in close contact with them and provide additional information as it becomes available. Thank you, Principal Roth" The Martin County Sheriff's Office said the investigation remains active and additional charges are possible.

entry.title: Martin County border collie hoarding case moves forward as 30 rescued dogs find new homes
entry.summary: A criminal case involving 36 rescued border collies in Martin County is moving forward. Paige O'Donnell faces 72 criminal charges two for each dog rescued from her home. She was not present at her docket sounding Thursday afternoon in the Martin County courthouse, but I spoke with her attorney, Russell Ferraro. WATCH BELOW: Rescued dogs find new homes in animal hoarding case Dogs rescued in suspected animal cruelty case find new homes 'At this point I can't really say anything on her behalf for or against her,' Ferraro said. 'We just got the discovery in the case yesterday. We're organizing it, going through it, and we'll take it from there.' It has been just under two months since Martin County deputies took 36 dogs out of O'Donnell's feces-filled home on Aug. 10. The county condemned it days after the Border Collies were rescued. Ferraro said O'Donnell is staying elsewhere while the house is under repair. O'Donnell faces an animal cruelty and improper confinement charge for each dog and has pleaded not guilty. 'Everybody's got a right to a fair trial and to due process,' Ferraro said. The next hearing in O'Donnell's case is scheduled for Dec. 1. While the outcome of the case remains uncertain, most of O'Donnell's former dogs have found loving homes. According to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast, 30 of the dogs have been adopted, five have gone or are about to go to animal rescues, and one remains up for adoption. 'She's just has an endless amount of energy and just wants to expend it at all times,' Cale said. entry.summary: Floridians who want to cast a ballot in the 2026 General Election have until Monday, Oct. 5, to register to vote or update their voter registration information. Voters are encouraged to verify that their registration details, including their name, address and party affiliation, are accurate before the deadline. Voters are also urged to confirm their Election Day polling location. Voter registration deadline is Oct. 5 for November election Election Day is scheduled for Tuesday, Nov. 3, with polls open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Residents can register to vote or update their registration online through Florida's voter registration website , by mail or in person using a Florida Voter Registration Application. Applications are also available at Supervisor of Elections Offices and other designated voter registration agencies. Key election deadlines Voter registration deadline: Monday, Oct. 5, 2026 Vote-by-mail request deadline: Thursday, Oct. 22, 2026, by 5 p.m. Early voting dates, locations Palm Beach County: Oct. 19-Nov. 1 from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Voters can cast their ballot at any of the 28 locations during this time. St. Lucie County: Oct. 1931 from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily, including Sunday, Oct. 25. The county will have eight early-voting locations across the county. Vote-by-mail ballots must be received by the Supervisor of Elections office by 7 p.m. Election Day to be counted and may be returned to a secure ballot intake station located at each early voting location during early voting hours, or in person to the Supervisor of Elections office. Okeechobee County: Oct. 24-31 from 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. at one location: 307 NW 5th Avenue in Okeechobee Election Day: Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026, from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Voters must cast their ballot at their assigned precinct.

entry.title: Dolphins rule out rookie WR Caleb Douglas for second straight week with ankle injury
entry.summary: The Miami Dolphins will be without rookie receiver Caleb Douglas for a second straight game as he continues nursing an ankle injury suffered in Week 2. Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Friday that Douglas and defensive end Robert Beal Jr. (hamstring) will miss Sunday's game at Minnesota, but Miami will have veteran center Aaron Brewer, who appeared on Thursday's injury report with a hand issue. 'He's in every meeting, and hes got to stay locked in, and hes got to watch practice, watch the practice tape, and stay on top of it,' Hafley said of Douglas missing what could be valuable reps early in the season, 'because what we dont want to have happen is when he gets back and hopefully thats soon that he takes a step back mentally. Hes doing a good job, hes a mature guy. Douglas, who has seven receptions for 117 yards in two games, has not practiced the past two weeks after suffering the injury in the second half of a loss at San Francisco. He was one of the standouts in the preseason and was expected to emerge as one of the top targets for quarterback Malik Willis. With Douglas sidelined, fellow rookie Chris Bell, who has still been ramping up from a knee injury suffered last year, had four receptions for 64 yards in last week's loss to Kansas City . Receiver Malik Washington had five catches for 56 yards, and tight end Greg Dulcich added five catches for 55 yards. Hafley said he wants to see improvement in the timing and rhythm with Willis' connection with his young receiving corps. entry.title: Altercation at tow yard leads to shooting, Martin County Sheriff's Office says - WPBF
entry.summary: Altercation at tow yard leads to shooting, Martin County Sheriff's Office says    WPBF
entry.article_text: Two Miami women are facing charges after an altercation led to a shooting Friday afternoon at Gary's Towing and Recovery near Stuart and a crash, the Martin County Sheriff's Office said. Jade Ely Brandon, 23, is facing two counts of aggravated assault with a firearm, discharging a firearm in public, aggravated fleeing and eluding, driving while license suspended and felony criminal mischief. Sheriff John Budensiek told WPBF's Ari Hait that Valerie Valdes, 22, caused a crash while fleeing and faces charges of operating an unregistered motorcycle vehicle and reckless driving with injuries. At 1 p.m., deputies responded to 4405 SE Cove Road. Brandon arrived at the tow yard to claim a vehicle that had been towed there earlier in the day. She appeared with Valdes, Budensiek said. A short time later, two other people showed up to pick up the same car. The four people started arguing and the Miami woman grabbed a gun and started shooting before getting into a vehicle and fleeing the area, the agency said. Budensiek said some of the bullets went into the trailer where tow yard employees were working. Budensiek said they are thankful employees and those involved are safe. “They're extremely fortunate just doing their job, minding their own business," the sheriff said. They've got a lot going on.” https://www.facebook.com/MartinCountySheriffsOffice/posts/pfbid0enPBfuxCWxva9Ce6vmU7hGP3nKdhfidsLzp1e7zxkZ58uSYxB3KhHPTdVi9kagZnl Because the tow yard is about a half-mile from Murray Middle School, the sheriff’s office activated an active-shooter response and placed the school on lockout as deputies responded to the scene. Road patrol deputies, aviation, detectives and other available units began searching for the suspect vehicle. Deputies located the vehicle traveling on Cove Road near U.S. 1 and attempted a traffic stop. The driver fled, and deputies performed a Precision Immobilization Technique, or PIT maneuver, bringing the vehicle to a stop, the MCSO said. Additional units moved in and successfully immobilized the vehicle before the driver could flee again. The individuals targeted by the gunfire had left the area before deputies arrived. At this time, it is unclear whether any of them were struck by gunfire, the agency said. entry.title: Martin County border collie hoarding case moves forward as 30 rescued dogs find new homes - WFLX
entry.summary: Martin County border collie hoarding case moves forward as 30 rescued dogs find new homes    WFLX
entry.article_text: A criminal case involving 36 rescued border collies in Martin County is moving forward. Paige O’Donnell faces 72 criminal charges — two for each dog rescued from her home. She was not present at her docket sounding Thursday afternoon in the Martin County courthouse, but I spoke with her attorney, Russell Ferraro. “At this point I can’t really say anything on her behalf for or against her,” Ferraro said. “We just got the discovery in the case yesterday. We’re organizing it, going through it, and we’ll take it from there.” It has been just under two months since Martin County deputies took 36 dogs out of O’Donnell’s feces-filled home on Aug. The county condemned it days after the Border Collies were rescued. Ferraro said O’Donnell is staying elsewhere while the house is under repair. O’Donnell faces an animal cruelty and improper confinement charge for each dog and has pleaded not guilty. “Everybody’s got a right to a fair trial and to due process,” Ferraro said. The next hearing in O’Donnell’s case is scheduled for Dec. While the outcome of the case remains uncertain, most of O’Donnell’s former dogs have found loving homes. According to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast, 30 of the dogs have been adopted, five have gone or are about to go to animal rescues, and one remains up for adoption. Lucie and Colleen Tilley near Deltona each adopted one of the rescued border collies. Both say their new family members — now named Nadia and Leila — have had little trouble adjusting to their new lives. “She’s just has an endless amount of energy and just wants to expend it at all times,” Cale said. Cale said Nadia, named after a character from the show “New Girl,” goes to work with him every day and usually warms up to new people after they offer her a treat. “She’s just has an endless amount of energy and just wants to expend it at all times,” Cale said. “When I saw where they came from, I expected a lot more of a challenge,” he added. She wants to be out there and interacting with the world.” “There’s no off switch; it’s all go, go, go,” Tilley said, as Leila raced back and forth behind her in her backyard during a Zoom interview. “It’s really satisfying to see, actually. Just that she’s— she’s happy.” Tilley recalled how nervous Leila was when she first came home on Sept. “At first — like the first three days — it took her to be able to go out the doors— like when I opened the front door, she would run and hide under the bed,” Tilley said. “Now she just runs straight through the sliding glass door, or into it.” Cale and Tilley both said their new border collies have taken well to training as they work to shed old habits, like jumping onto countertops. “I think that’s how they got their food,” Tilley speculated. When Tilley thinks about the criminal case against Leila’s former owner, she wonders what went wrong. Tilley, who showed dogs with her family during her childhood, said she remembers O’Donnell and her outstanding reputation. Like she had very well-bred dogs, very well-trained dogs, beautiful dogs,” Tilley said. “And so all of us were just like, what happened?” Cale revealed that he’d been grieving the loss of his beloved Border Collie, Jessie, who’d died from cancer a year before he heard about what had happened in Palm City. “You just never know when the right dog is gonna come along, and this was the right dog,” Cale said. “(Jessie) was the ride-or-die that would have gone anywhere with me — roaming the woods and getting into mischief ... And that’s gonna be Nadia now.” “You just never know when the right dog is gonna come along, and this was the right dog,” Cale said. The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast says one Border Collie is still up for adoption. entry.title: 'I get chewed to death': St. Lucie County tackles mosquito breeding after heavy rain - WPBF
entry.summary: 'I get chewed to death': St. Lucie County tackles mosquito breeding after heavy rain    WPBF
entry.article_text: Lucie County mosquito control are working to stop mosquitoes from breeding after recent rain created standing water. In a residential neighborhood near U.S. 1 and Fort Pierce, mosquito control teams treated swales and used a backpack blower to distribute larvicide. Officials said the rain has increased standing water, which allows mosquito eggs to hatch. "So relative to last year, mosquito calls have been pretty reduced, but at any moment’s notice following a lot of rain, we can have a huge strike in population, so it's important to be on top of our game," said Daniel Tuzzolino, senior entomologist at St. Lucie County Mosquito Control. DENGUE FEVER: Dengue fever case in Palm Beach County prompts mosquito control action Kenneth Fusco, a nearby resident, shared his experience with the mosquito problem. "If I go out in my front yard and start to do anything, you get bit. I have an island behind me with some cats. If I go over there, I have to wear long pants because I get chewed to death," Fusco said. He added, "Park the truck and leave it for 20 minutes and leave it in front of my house, please!" Crews are also monitoring reports of dengue fever and West Nile virus in surrounding counties. They are asking residents to empty or remove containers holding water to prevent mosquito breeding. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates "We are really doubling down and making sure that the people of St. Lucie County know the importance of tipping and tossing because anything that you do to remove potential environment for those dangerous mosquitoes really helps reduce the likelihood that we have transmission in this county," Tuzzolino said. Thursday's heavy rain also caused erosion and a washout along Indian River Drive, where crews were completing a shoulder repair project designed to protect the roadway during heavy rain events. More rain is expected, which could lead to additional standing water and, Tuzzolino said, "A lot more mosquitoes! A lot more mosquitoes!" If you are dealing with a mosquito problem near your home, contact St. Lucie County mosquito control at 772-462-1962 or email mosquito@stlucieco.org.
